# 逐棒读图

### 价格行为技术分析（给严肃交易者的读图课）

**Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar**
The Technical Analysis of Price Action for the Serious Trader

作者：**阿尔·布鲁克斯（Al Brooks）**

---

- 英文原版：John Wiley & Sons, Inc.（Wiley Trading 系列），2009 年；ISBN 978-0-470-44395-8
- 结构：15 章（价格行为 → 趋势线与通道 → 趋势 → 回调 → 区间 → 突破 → 磁力位 → 趋势反转 →
  小级别反转：失败形态 → 日内交易 → 开盘第一小时 → 日内交易实例 → 日/周/月线 → 期权 → 最佳交易）
- 图表：全部采用 **Wiley 官方图库原图**（TIF 原图，275 张；其中图 15.21 官方图库缺图，
  用原书页内图补足），图内标注是 TradeStation 的英文标注，保留原样，另附《附录 B · 图内标注对照表》
- 本译本：依据英文原版全文翻译的**中文精校本**；中文版与中英对照版并行
- 底稿来源：原书是 2009 年的扫描件，文本层为 Acrobat ClearScan（旧 OCR，含 `AI Brooks`、
  `FIGURE 1 1 . 1`、`I-minute` 之类误识）。本译本对全书做了**双 OCR 清洗**：
  ClearScan 文本层与 RapidOCR(300 dpi) 逐块比对，逐 token 仲裁（文字信 ClearScan、数字信 RapidOCR），
  分歧处再回看 600 dpi 页面图像第三次识别；图注按官方图号表逐张核对（275 张全部对上）。


# 译者说明

## 一、这本书是什么

《逐棒读图》（*Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar*，2009）是阿尔·布鲁克斯的第一本书，也是他后来那套
《高级趋势技术分析》《高级波段技术分析》《高级反转技术分析》三部曲的**源头**。全书 15 章，
讲的是一件事：**把图一根K线一根K线地读下来**，从每一根K线里读出多空谁在控盘、接下来大概率往哪边走。

| 章 | 主题 |
|---|---|
| 第 1 章 | 价格行为（全书方法总纲：趋势K线、十字星、信号K线、入场K线、外包K线、收盘价的意义） |
| 第 2 章 | 趋势线与趋势通道（含微型趋势线、水平线、决斗线） |
| 第 3 章 | 趋势 |
| 第 4 章 | 回调 |
| 第 5 章 | 交易区间 |
| 第 6 章 | 突破 |
| 第 7 章 | 磁力位 |
| 第 8 章 | 趋势反转 |
| 第 9 章 | 小级别反转：失败形态 |
| 第 10 章 | 日内交易 |
| 第 11 章 | 开盘第一小时 |
| 第 12 章 | 日内交易实例 |
| 第 13 章 | 日线图、周线图与月线图 |
| 第 14 章 | 期权 |
| 第 15 章 | 最佳交易 |

书末另有作者的《交易准则》（20 条）与原书术语表，本书一并译出。

## 二、术语口径

本书与三部曲共用同一套**四书统一术语表**（见附录 A，225 条）：

- 术语以「**清晰、无歧义**」为最高准则，而不是照搬任何一种既有译法；
- 同一英文词在全书只有一个中文对应词：`signal bar` 一律「信号K线」，`spike` 一律「急速行情」，
  `measured move` 一律「等距运动」，`trader's equation` 一律「交易者等式」，`always-in` 一律「始终入场」；
- `leg` 译「行情段」、`swing` 译「波段」，两个高频词不共用一个中文词；
- `failure` 在第 9 章指**失败形态**（突破/信号/目标没兑现），不译成「错误」或「缺陷」；
- 本书特有的 `Trend from the Open` 译**开盘即趋势**、`2HM` 首现写作「2HM（两小时未触均线）」。

## 三、图与图号

- 图表全部使用 **Wiley 官方图库原图**（275 张，未压缩、未重绘）；官方图库缺图 15.21，用原书页内图补足。
- 图内标注是 TradeStation 的英文标注（`H1`、`L2`、`ii`、`ioi`、`BO`、`EMA` 等），**保留原样**，
  另以《附录 B · 图内标注对照表》一次性说明读法。
- **图号与英文原版完全一致**（`图 4.13` 就是原书 Figure 4.13），永不重编，便于与原版逐图对照。

## 四、底稿与清洗（本书特有）

原书是 2009 年的扫描件，PDF 文本层是 Acrobat ClearScan 的旧 OCR，存在三类系统性错误：

1. 图号被拆：`FIGURE 1 1 . 1`（应为 1.1）、`FIGURE I . I S`（应为 1.18）、`FIGURE • . • 7`（应为 1.17）；
2. 数字与字母混淆：`I-minute`（应为 1-minute）、`1 5-rninute`（应为 15-minute）、`AI Brooks`（应为 Al Brooks）；
3. 单词误识与跨行断词：`aXtive`（active）、`fonned`（formed）、`nOITIlally`（normally）等。

本译本的清洗流程：**ClearScan 文本层与 RapidOCR(300 dpi) 逐块比对**，逐 token 仲裁
（文字以 ClearScan 为准、数字以 RapidOCR 为准），仍有分歧的块回看 **600 dpi 页面图像做第三次识别**；
图注按官方图号表逐张核对，275 张全部对上。清洗过程中的分歧与判定记录在 `qa/` 目录。

## 五、给读者的提示

- 原书所有时间均为**美国东部/中部时间**，作者用的是 PST（太平洋时间）；书中时间未做换算。
- 图上标的 `H1/L2/ii/ioi` 是作者自己的计数法：**高1/低1** 指趋势中第一次回撤后的入场点，
  **高2/低2** 指第二次；数字越大，说明多空拉锯越多。读图时对着《附录 B》看即可。
- 本书的观点是作者的个人经验，不构成任何投资建议。


# 前言

*Preface*


我写这本书的目的，是讲清楚我为什么认为图 P.1中的那些交易有着极佳的风险回报比，并给出一些方法，让大家在股票和期货交易中都能从这类建仓形态里获利。我能传达的最重要的一点是：只盯最出色的那几笔交易，避开最差的那些建仓形态，同时努力提高你每次交易的股数。我坦然承认，我为每个建仓形态给出的理由都只是我个人的看法，我对某笔交易为什么能成的推理可能完全是错的。不过，这并不重要。重要的是，逐棒读图是一种非常有效的交易方式，而我对某些事情为什么会那样发生做过大量思考。我对自己的解释感到踏实，它们在我下单时给了我信心，但它们与我下单这件事无关，所以它们对不对对我不重要。正如我可以在瞬间反转自己对市场方向的看法，只要我遇到一个更合乎逻辑的理由，或者发现自己的逻辑有漏洞，我也同样可以反转自己对某个特定形态为什么有效的看法。我把这些看法讲出来，是因为它们看起来说得通，也可能会帮读者在交易某些建仓形态时更踏实，还因为它们可能颇具启发性，但任何一笔价格行为交易都并不需要它们。


> My goals in writing this book are to describe my understanding of why the trades in Figure P.1 offer great risk-reward ratios, and to present ways to profit from setups like these in both stocks and futures trading. The most important message that I can deliver is to focus on the absolute best trades, avoid the absolute worst setups, and work on increasing the number of shares that you are trading. I freely recognize that every one of my reasons behind each setup is just my opinion and my reasoning about why a trade works might be completely wrong. However, that is irrelevant. What is important is that reading price action is a very effective way to trade, and I have thought a lot about why certain things happen the way that they do. I am comfortable with my explanations, and they give me confidence when I place a trade, but they are irrelevant to my placing trades, so it is not important to me that they are right. Just as I can reverse my opinion about the direction of the market in an instant, I . can also reverse my opinion about why a particular pattern works if I come across a reason that is more logical or if I discover a flaw in my logic. I am providing the opinions because they appear to make sense, and they may help readers become more comfortable trading certain setups and because they may be intellectually stimulating, but they are not needed for any price action trades.


**图 P.1　AAPL，截至2008年6月10日的日线图（这张加了趋势线的图也出现在最后一章，并附有每笔交易背后的解释。）**


本书是一本全面理解价格行为的指南，面向经验丰富的交易者和市场专业人士。不过，这些概念对各个水平的交易者都同样有用。书中采用了爱德华兹与迈吉以及许多其他人描述过的许多标准技术，但会更侧重单根K线，以展示它们所提供的信息如何能显著提高交易的风险回报比。大多数书只在一张图上指出三四笔交易，言外之意是图上的其他一切都不可理解、没有意义或者风险太大。我相信，一天中发生的每一个最小报价单位里都有值得学习的东西，每张图上的好交易都远不止那几笔显而易见的，但要想看见它们，你必须理解价格行为，不能把任何K线当作无关紧要而忽略掉。我在显微镜下做过几千次操作，从中学到的是：最重要的东西有时可以非常微小。


> The book is a comprehensive guide to understanding price action and is directed toward sophisticated traders and market professionals. However, the concepts are useful to traders at all levels. It uses many of the standard techniques described by Edwards and Magee and many others, but will focus more on individual bars to demonstrate how the information they provide can significantly enhance the risk-reward ratio of trading. Most books point out three or four trades on a chart, which implies that everything else on the chart is incomprehensible, meaningless, or risky. I believe that there is something to be learned from every tick that takes place during the day and that there are far more great trades on every chart than just the few obvious ones, but to see them, you have to understand price action, and you cannot dismiss any bars as unimportant. I learned from performing thousands of operations through a microscope that some of the most important things can be very small.


我一根一根K线地读图，寻找每根K线告诉我的任何信息。它们全都重要。每根K线结束时，多数交易者都会问自己：“刚刚发生了什么？”对大多数K线，他们的结论是实在太难理解，于是选择去等一个自己认得的形态。这就好像他们认定这根K线不存在，或者把它当作机构的程序化操作而一笔勾销，认为个人交易者做不了。在这些时候，他们感觉自己不属于市场的一部分，可这些时候构成了交易日中的绝大部分时间。然而，只要看一眼成交量，他们忽略掉的所有那些K线，成交量与那些被他们拿来当作交易依据的K线一样大。显然，大量的交易正在发生，可他们不明白这怎么可能，于是基本上就当它不存在。但这等于否认现实。交易始终在发生，作为交易者，你有责任去理解它为什么发生，并想办法从中赚钱。弄清市场在告诉你什么，非常耗时、非常困难，但它给你的是成为成功交易者所需的基础。


> I read charts bar by bar and look for any information that each bar is telling me. They are all important. At the end of every bar, most traders ask themselves, "What just took place?" With most bars, they conclude that it is just too confusing to understand and choose to wait for a pattern that they recognize. It is as if they believe that the bar did not exist, or they dismiss it as just institutional program activity that is not tradable by an individual trader. They do not feel as though they are part of the market at these times, but these times constitute the vast majority of the day. Yet, if they look at the volume, all of those bars that they are ignoring have as much volume as the bars they are using for the bases for their trades. Clearly, a lot of trading is taking place, but they don't understand how that can be, and essentially they pretend that it does not exist. But that is denying reality. There is always trading taking place, and as a trader you owe it to yourself to understand why it's taking place and to figure out a way to make money off it. Learning what the market is telling you is very time consuming and difficult, but it gives you the foundation that you need to be a successful trader.


大多数讲蜡烛图的书，多数读者都会忍不住去死记形态，本书则不同，它会给出理由，说明某些形态为什么是可靠的建仓形态。书中有些术语对市场技术人员有特定含义，对交易者却是另一种含义，而这本书完全是站在交易者的角度写的。我确信许多交易者早就懂本书里的一切，只是很可能不会像我这样描述价格行为。成功的交易者之间没有秘密，他们都熟悉常见的建仓形态，许多人还给每一种起了自己的名字。他们几乎都在同一时间买进卖出，把握同一批波段，每个人都有自己的入场理由。许多人凭直觉做价格行为交易，从不觉得有必要说清某个建仓形态为什么有效。我希望他们读我这份对价格行为的理解与视角时读得开心，也希望这能给他们一些启发，让他们本已成功的交易更上一层楼。


> Unlike most books on candle charts where the majority of readers feel compelled to memorize patterns, this book will provide a rationale for why particular patterns are reliable setups for traders. Some of the terms used have specific meaning to market technicians but different meanings to traders and I am writing this entirely from a trader's perspective. I ;;un certain tp.at many traders already understand everything in this book, but likely wouldn't describe price action in the same way that I do. There are no secrets among successful traders, and they all know common setups, and many have their own names for each one. All of them are buying and selling pretty much at the same time, catching the same swings, and each has his own reasons for getting into a trade. Many trade price action intuitively without ever feeling a need to articulate why a certain setup works. I hope that they enjoy reading my understanding of and perspective on price action and that this gives them some insights that will improve their already successful trading.


大多数交易者的目标，是通过一种与自身性格相容的风格来把交易利润最大化。没有这种相容性，我认为想长期盈利地交易几乎是不可能的。许多交易者想知道自己要用多久才能成功，并且愿意亏上一段时间，甚至亏几年。可我是花了10年以上才能成功交易的。我们每个人都有自己的种种顾虑和分心事，所以这个时间长短因人而异，但交易者必须在做到稳定盈利之前解决掉大部分障碍。我有几个必须纠正的大问题，其中包括养育三个可爱的女儿，她们总让我的脑子里装满她们的影子以及身为父亲该做的事。这个问题随着她们长大、越来越独立而解决了。然后我花了很长时间才接受自己的许多性格特点是真实的、改不掉的（或者至少我得出结论：我不愿意改）。最后还有信心问题。我在那么多事情上一直自信到近乎傲慢，认识我的人要是知道这对我来说居然很难，一定会吃惊。但在内心深处，我相信自己永远也拿不出一套既能稳定盈利、又让我愿意用上许多年的方法。于是我买了许多系统，编写并测试了数不清的指标和系统，读了许多书和杂志，去听讲座，请家教，加入聊天室，和那些自称成功交易者的人交谈，但我从没看过他们的账户对账单，并且怀疑其中大多数人教得了、能做的却寥寥无几。交易里通常是这样：懂的人不说，说的人不懂。


> The goal for most traders is to maximize trading profits through a style that is compatible with their personalities. Without that compatibility, I believe that it is virtually impossible to trade profitably long term. Many traders wonder how long it will take them to be successful and are willing to lose money for some period of time, even a few years. However, it took me over 10 years to be able to trade successfully. Each of us has many considerations and distractions, so the time will vary, but a trader has to work though most obstacles before becoming consistently profitable. I had several major problems that had to be corrected, including raising three wonderful daughters who always filled my mind with thoughts of them and what I needed to be doing as their father. That was solved as they got older and more independent. Then it took me a long time to accept many personality traits as real and unchangeable (or at least I concluded that I was unwilling to change them). And finally there was the issue of confidence. I have always been confident to the point of arrogant in so many things that those who know me would be surprised that this was difficult for me. However, deep inside I believed that I really would never come up with a consistently profitable approach that I would enjoy employing for many years. Instead, I bought many systems, wrote and tested countless indicators and systems, read many books and magazines, went to seminars, hired tutors, joined chat rooms, and talked with people who presented themselves as successful traders, but I never saw their account statements and suspect that most could teach but few if any could trade. Usually in trading, those who know don't talk, and those who talk don't know.


这一切都极有帮助，因为它让我看清了在成功之前所有必须避开的东西。任何不做交易的人看一眼图表，都会不由自主要地得出结论：交易必定极其简单，而这正是它的吸引力之一。一天下来，任何人都能看着任何一张图，看出非常清晰的进出场点。然而，在实时行情里这么做要难得多。人有一种天然的倾向，总想买在最低的那个点上，并且指望行情再也不回来。一旦行情回来了，新手就会止损以避免更大的亏损，结果是一连串亏损交易，最终把他的账户打爆。用宽止损能在一定程度上解决这个问题，但交易者迟早还是会撞上几笔大亏，账户变红，吓得再也不敢用这套方法。


> This was all extremely helpful because it showed all of the things that I needed to avoid before becoming successful. Any nontrader who looks at a chart will invariably conclude that trading has to be extremely easy, and that is part of the appeal. At the end of the day, anyone can look at any chart and see very clear entry and exit points. However, it is much more difficult to do in real time. There is a natural tendency to want to buy the exact low and never have the trade come back. If it does, a novice will take the loss to avoid a bigger loss, resulting in a series of losing trades that will ultimately bust his account. Using wide stops solves that to some extent, but invariably a trader will soon hit a few big losses that will put him into the red and make him too scared to continue using that approach.


为什么这么多商学院至今仍推荐爱德华兹与迈吉，尽管他们的书本质上相当简单，主要用趋势线、突破和回调作为交易的基础？他们这么做，是因为这套体系有效，过去一直有效，将来也永远有效。如今几乎所有的交易者都有电脑、能拿到日内数据，那些技术中有许多都可以改用到日内交易上。此外，蜡烛图还能提供额外信息，说明是谁在控制市场，从而带来更及时的入场和更小的风险。爱德华兹与迈吉关注的是整体趋势。我用的是同样的基本技术，但会更仔细地观察图上单根的K线，以提高风险回报比，并且对日内图着墨相当多。


> Why do so many business schools continue to recommend Edwards and Magee when their book is essentially simplistic, largely using trendlines, breakouts, and pullbacks as the basis for trading? They do so because the system works, and it always has, and it always will. Now that just about all traders have computers with access to intraday data, many of those techniques can be adapted to day trading. Also, candle charts give additional information about who is controlling the market, which results in a more timely entry with smaller risk. Edwards and Magee's focus is on the overall trend. I use those same basic techniques but pay much closer attention to the individual bars on the chart to improve the risk-reward ratio, and I devote considerable attention to intraday charts.


在我看来有一点显而易见：如果一个人能把图读得足够好，好到能在行情即将起飞且不再回头的那一刻精确入场，那这个交易者就会拥有巨大的优势。他的胜率会很高，少数几次亏损也会很小。我决定把这当作我的起点，而我的发现是：什么额外的东西都不需要加。事实上，任何添加都是干扰，只会拉低盈利能力。这话听上去太显然、太简单，以至于大多数人很难相信。


> It seemed obvious to me that if one could simply read the charts well enough to be able to enter at the exact times that the move would take off and not come back, then that trader would have a huge advantage. He would have a high winning percentage and the few losses would be small. I decided that this would be my starting point, and what I discovered was that nothing had to be added. In fact, any additions are distractions that result in lower profitability. This sounds so obvious and easy that it is difficult for most people to believe.


我是个日内交易者，完全依赖 Emini 标普500期货（下称“Emini”）日内图上的价格行为，而且我相信，读好价格行为对所有交易者来说都是一项无价的技能。初学者反倒常常有一种根深蒂固的信念：还需要更多的东西，也许某个鲜有人用的复杂数学公式，才能给他们正好需要的那点优势。高盛那么有钱、那么老练，一定有一台超级计算机和威力强大的软件，那优势足以确保所有个人交易者注定失败。于是他们开始看各种各样的指标，玩各种参数，把指标调得恰到好处。每个指标都有一些时候管用，但对我来说，它们非但没有讲清楚，反而把事情搞模糊了。事实上，你就算完全不看图表，随便下个买单，也有50% 的概率是对的！


> I am a day trader who relies entirely on price action on the intraday Emini S&P 500 Futures (the "Emini") charts, and I believe that reading price action well is an invaluable skill for all traders. Beginners often instead have a deep-seated belief that something more is required, that maybe some complex mathematical formula that very few use would give them just the edge that they need. Goldman Sachs is so rich and sophisticated that they must have a supercomputer and high-powered software that gives them an advantage that insures that all the individual traders are doomed to failure. They start looking at all kinds of indicators and playing with the inputs to customize the indicators to make them just right. Every indicator works some of the time, but for me, they obfuscate instead of elucidate. In fact, without even looking at a chart, you can place a buy order and have a 50 percent chance of being right!


我并不是因为不懂指标的微妙之处才否定指标和系统。多年来，我在编写和测试指标与系统上花了超过10,000个小时，这大概远超大多数人的经验。这段与指标和系统打交道的丰富经历，是我成为成功交易者的必经一环。指标对许多交易者很管用，但最大的成功来自交易者找到一种与自己性格相容的方法。我对指标和系统的最大问题，是我从未完全信任它们。每一个建仓形态面前，我都能看到需要检验的例外。我总是想从市场里榨出最后一块钱，只要我能加一点新花样让它更好，就永远不满足于一套系统的收益。我就是太爱控制、太强迫、太躁动、太爱观察、太不信任别人，靠指标或自动化系统根本赚不到长期的钱，但我在很多方面都处在极端，大多数人并没有我这些问题。


> I am not dismissing indicators and systems out of ignorance of their subtleties. I have spent over 10,000 hours writing and testing indicators and systems over the years, and that probably is far more experience than most. This extensive experience with indicators and systems was an essential part of my becoming a successful trader. Indicators work well for many traders, but the best success comes once a trader finds an approach that is compatible with his personality. My single biggest problem with indicators and systems is that I never fully trusted them. At every setup, I saw exceptions that needed to be tested. I always wanted every last penny out of the market and was never satisfied with a return from a system if I could incorporate a new twist that would make it better. I am simply too controlling, compulsive, restless, observant, and untrusting to make money long term off indicators or automated systems, but I am at the extreme in many ways, and most people don't have these same issues.


许多交易者，尤其是初学者，会被指标吸引，指望指标告诉他们何时该入场。他们没意识到的是，绝大多数指标都建立在简单的价格行为之上；而在我下单的时候，我根本来不及思考好几个指标可能同时在告诉我的东西。另外，振荡指标往往让交易者去寻找反转，对价格图的关注就少了。在市场每天有两三次、每次持续一小时以上的反转时，这些工具可以很管用。问题出在市场强势趋势的时候。如果你太盯指标，你会看到它们整天都在形成背离，结果可能发现自己一再逆势入场、一再亏钱。等你终于接受市场正在趋势中时，当天剩下的时间已经不够你回本了。反过来说，如果你只是看着K线图或蜡烛图，你会看到市场明显在趋势中，也就不会被指标引诱去找趋势反转。最常见的成功反转，先由强动能突破一条趋势线，再回调测试极端点；而一个交易者如果太盯背离，往往就会忽略这个根本事实。没有逆势动能推动趋势线被突破，单凭背离就是一个亏钱的策略。等趋势线被突破，再看对旧极端点的测试是反转，还是原趋势恢复。在这里一次强反转是高概率交易，至少做剥头皮是如此，你并不需要指标来告诉你这一点，而且几乎肯定会有背离，那你又何必把指标加进你的推算、把思考搞复杂？


> Many traders, especially beginners, are drawn to indicators, hoping that an indicator will show them when to enter a trade. What they don't realize is that the vast majority of indicators are based on simple price action, and when I am placing trades, I simply cannot think fast enough to process what several indicators might be telling me. Also, oscillators tend to make traders look for reversals and focus less on price charts. These can be effective tools on most days when the market has two or three reversals lasting an hour or more. The problem comes when the market is trending strongly. If you focus too much on your indicators, you will see that they are forming divergences all day long, and you may find yourself repeatedly entering Countertrend and losing money. By the time you come to accept that the market is trending, you will not have enough time left in the day to recoup your losses. Instead, if you were simply looking at a bar or candle chart, you would see that the market is clearly trending, and you would not be tempted by indicators to look for trend reversals. The most common successful reversals first break a trendline with strong momentum and then pullback to test the extreme, and if a trader focuses too much on divergences, she will often overlook this fundamental fact. A divergence in the absence of a Countertrend momentum surge that breaks a trendline is a losing strategy. Wait for the trendline break, and then see if the test of the old extreme reverses or if the old trend resumes. You do not need an indicator to tell you that a strong reversal here is a high-probability trade, at least for a scalp, and there will almost certainly be a divergence, so why complicate your thinking by adding the indicator to your calculus?


有些评论者推荐把多个时间级别、指标、数浪以及斐波那契回撤与扩展组合起来使用，可真到下这笔交易的时候，他们只有在出现一个好的价格行为建仓形态时才会动手。同样，当他们看到一个好的价格行为建仓形态时，又会开始找显示背离的指标，或者换不同时间级别去等均线测试、数浪或斐波那契形态来确认眼前的东西。实际上，他们就是价格行为交易者，只在一张图上、完全靠价格行为交易，只是不愿意痛快承认罢了。他们把交易复杂化到了这种程度：过度分析占用了太多下单所需的时间，许多许多交易必然错过，只能被迫去等下一个建仓形态。把简单的东西搞得如此复杂，道理上是讲不通的。当然，增加任何信息都可能带来更好的决策，许多人在决定要不要下单时，或许也能处理大量输入。仅凭一种简单化的意识形态就无视数据，那是愚蠢的。目标是赚钱，交易者应该尽一切努力把自己的利润最大化。只是我在准确下单所需的时间内，确实处理不好多个指标和多个时间级别，而我发现，仔细读一张图对我来说盈利要多得多。另外，一旦依赖指标，我发现自己的价格行为读图就变懒了，常常漏掉明摆着的东西。价格行为远比任何其他信息都重要，如果你为了从别处获取信息而牺牲掉价格行为正在告诉你的一部分内容，你很可能就是在做一个糟糕的决定。


> Some pundits recommend a combination of time frames, indicators, wave counting, and Fibonacci retracements and extensions, but when it comes time to place the trade, they will only do it if there is a good price action setup. Also, when they see a good price action setup, they start looking for indicators that show divergences or different time frames for moving average tests or wave counts or Fibonacci setups to confirm what is in front of them. In reality, they are price action traders who are trading exclusively off price action on only one chart but don't feel comfortable admitting it. They are complicating their trading to the point that they certainly are missing many, many trades because their overanalysis takes too much time to place their orders, and they are forced to wait for the next setup. The logic just isn't there for making the simple so complicated. Obviously adding any information can lead to better decision making, and many people may be able to process lots of inputs when deciding whether to place a trade. Ignoring data because of a simplistic ideology alone is foolish. The goal is to make money, and a trader should do everything he can to maximize his profits. I simply cannot process multiple indicators and time frames well in the time needed to place my orders accurately, and I find that carefully reading a single chart is far more profitable for me. Also, if I rely on indicators, I find that I get lazy in my price action reading and often miss the obvious. Price action is far more important than any other information, and if you sacrifice some of what it is telling you to gain information from something else, you are likely making a bad decision.


交易股票和 Emini 有数不清的赚钱方式，但它们全都需要行情有波动（嗯，做空期权除外）。如果你学会读图，每天都能抓到大量这样的盈利交易，既不需要知道是哪家机构启动的趋势，也不需要知道任何指标在显示什么。你不需要他们的软件或分析师，因为他们会把自己的动作展示给你。你要做的只是搭上他们的便车，就能赚到钱。价格行为会告诉你他们在做什么，并让你能带着很紧的止损早早入场。


> There are countless ways to make money trading stocks and Eminis, but all require movement (well, except for shorting options). If you learn to read the charts, you will catch a great number of these profitable trades every day without ever knowing why some institution started the trend and without ever knowing what any indicator is showing. You don't need their software or analysts because they will show you what they are doing. All you have to do is piggy-back onto their trades, and you will make a profit. Price action will tell you what they are doing and allow you an early entry with a tight stop.


我发现，尽量减少下单时要考虑的东西，我反而能持续赚到多得多的钱。我需要的只是笔记本电脑上的单张图，除了20根K线的指数移动平均线之外不带任何指标，这条均线不需要太多分析，却每一天都能理清许多好的建仓形态。我有时连这条均线都不用也照样交易，但它给出的建仓形态足够多，通常值得留在图上。1分钟图上的成交量，在寻找趋势反转可能即将来临的迹象时有时也有一点点用，但我从不看它，因为我做的主要是不在5分钟图上交易（偶尔我会基于1分钟图做一次5分钟图的早入场）。异常巨大的1分钟成交量常常出现在空头趋势的末尾，接下来新出现的摆动低点或两个低点常常提供可获利的做多剥头皮机会。不过，这只是一点观察，它太不可靠，不能作为你交易的一部分，应当忽略。当抛售过度时，日线图上有时也会出现成交量的急速放大。


> I have found that I consistently make far more money by minimizing what I have to consider when placing a trade. All I need is a single chart on my laptop computer with no indicators except a 20-bar exponential moving average, which does not require too much analysis and clarifies many good setups each day. I sometimes trade even without the moving average, but it provides enough setups that it is usually worth having on the chart. Volume on 1-minute charts is also sometimes minimally useful when looking for a sign that a trend reversal might be imminent, but I never look at it because I trade mostly offt,he 5-minute chart (rarely I will take an early 5-minute With spike often comes near the end of a bear trend, and the next new swing Trend entry off the 1-minute chart). An unusually large 1-minute volume low or two often provide profitable long scalps. However, this is simply an observation; it is far too unreliable to be a part of your trading and should be ignored. Volume spikes also sometimes occur on daily charts when a sell off is overdone.


就连那些依据一组指标做交易的交易者，在下单和出场时也照样会看价格行为。如果在低点同时还有一根强反转K线，谁买这个背离会不觉得更踏实呢？不过，图表所提供的关于谁在掌控市场的信息，远远超过多数交易者意识到的程度。几乎每根K线都给出了市场将去向何方的重要线索，而一个把任何活动都当作噪音打发掉的交易者，每天都在放过许多可获利的交易。


> Even traders who base their trades on a collection of indicators routinely look at price action when placing their entries and exits. Who wouldn't feel better about buying a divergence if there was also a strong reversal bar at the low? However, charts provide far more information about who is in control of the market than most traders realize. Almost every bar offers important clues as to where the market is going, and a trader who dismisses any activity as noise is passing up many profitable trades each day.


作为一个交易者，我看什么都带着灰度，而且我一直在按概率思考。如果一个形态正在形成，它并不完美，但与可靠的建仓形态已经足够接近，那它很可能也会有类似的表现。接近通常就足够接近了〔译注：原文 “Close is usually close enough” 一语双关，close 兼指“接近”与“收盘价”。〕。如果某个东西看起来像教科书里的建仓形态，这笔交易的展开就很可能会与那个教科书建仓形态的交易相似。这就是交易的艺术，要在灰色地带里做好交易得花上好几年。人人都想要具体、明确的规则或指标，以及聊天室、通讯、热线或家教来告诉他们究竟何时入场，从而把风险最小化、利润最大化，但长远来看这些全都没用。你必须为自己的决定负责，但你首先得学会怎么做决定，而那意味着你得习惯在灰色迷雾里操作。没有什么事情像黑白那样分明，我做这行够久，已经领会到：任何事情，无论多么不可能，都可能发生，而且终将发生。这就像量子物理。每一个可以想象的事件都有概率，你还没考虑过的事件也一样有概率。它不情绪化，某件事为什么发生也无关紧要。盯着看美联储今天会不会降息是浪费时间，因为他们做的任何事都能有多头解读，也都能有空头解读。关键是要看市场怎么做，而不是美联储怎么做。交易时段内绝不要看消息。如果你想知道某条消息意味着什么，你眼前的图会告诉你。如果 CNBC 上某个评论者宣布某份报告是利空的，而市场却上涨，你会去做空吗？只看图，它会告诉你你需要知道的。图表才是给你钱或拿走你钱的那个东西，所以它才是交易时唯一该考虑的东西。如果你在交易大厅里，你连最好的朋友在做什么都不能信。他可能一边挂出大量橙汁看涨期权，一边私下让经纪商在场价下方等着买入十倍的数量。你那位朋友只是想制造一场恐慌把市场打下来，好让他通过一个中间人以好得多的价格大量建仓。


> As a trader, I see everything in shades of gray and am constantly thinking in terms of probabilities. If a pattern is setting up and it is not perfect but it is reasonably similar to a reliable setup, it will likely behave similarly as well. Close is usually close enough. If something resembles a textbook setup, the trade will likely unfold similarly to the trade from the textbook setup. This is the art of trading, and it takes years to become good at trading in the gray zone. Everyone wants concrete, clear rules, or indicators, and chat rooms, newsletters, hotlines, or tutors that will tell them when exactly to get in to minimize risk and maximize profit, but none of it works in the long run. You have to take responsibility for your decisions, but you first have to learn how to make them, and that means that you have to get used to operating in the gray fog. Nothing is ever as clear as black and white, and I have been doing this long enough to appreciate that anything, no matter how unlikely, can and will happen. It's like quantum physics. Every conceivable event has a probability, and so do events that you have yet to consider. It is not emotional, and the reasons why something happens are irrelevant. Watching to see if the Feds cut rates today is a waste of time because there is both a bullish and bearish interpretation of anything that they do. What is key is to see what the market does, not what the Fed does. Never watch the news during the trading day. If you want to know what a news event means, the chart in front of you will tell you. If a pundit on CNBC announces that a report was bearish and the market goes up, are you going to look to short? Only look at the chart, and it will tell you what you need to know. The chart is what will give you money or take money from you, so it is the only thing that you should ever consider when trading. If you are on the floor, you can't even trust what your best friend is doing. He might be offering a lot of orange juice calls but secretly having a broker looking to buy 10 times as many below the market. Your friend is just trying to create a panic to drive the market down so he can load up through a surrogate at a much better price.


消息还有一个问题。每当市场出现巨幅波动，记者们总能找到某位自信满满、极具说服力的专家，据说他预测到了这一切，然后去采访他，让观众以为这位评论者有一种预测市场的神秘能力，而背后那个不为人知的现实是：这位评论者最近10次预测全都错了。接着这位评论者又会做出对未来的某个预测，天真的观众就会赋予它重要意义，并让它影响自己的交易。观众可能没有意识到，有些评论者100% 的时候都看多，另一些100% 的时候都看空，还有一些则永远在挥棒搏全垒打，净做出离谱的预测。记者只是冲向那个与当天消息恰好一致的人，而这对交易者毫无用处。事实上它是有破坏性的，因为它会影响你的交易，让你怀疑并偏离自己的方法。所以，如果你实在必须在交易时段看电视，我推荐看动画片或者外语节目，这样节目就绝没有机会影响你的交易。


> There is one other problem with the news. Invariably when the market makes a huge move, the reporters will find some confident, convincing expert who predicted it and interview him, leading the viewers to believe that this pundit has an uncanny ability to predict the market, despite the untold reality that this same pundit has been wrong in his last 10 predictions. The pundit then makes some future prediction, and the naive viewer will attach significance to it and let it affect his trading. What the viewer may not realize is that some pundits are bullish 100 percent of the time and others are bearish 100 percent of the time, and still others just swing for the fences all of the time and make outrageous predictions. The reporter just rushes to the one who is consistent with the day's news, which is totally useless to a trader. In fact it is destructive because it can influence his trading and make him question and deviate from his own methods. So, if you really must watch TV during the trading day, I recommend cartoons or foreign language shows, so there will be no chance that the show will influence your trading.


朋友和同事会大方地提供意见供你忽略。偶尔会有交易者告诉我，他们有个很棒的建仓形态，想和我讨论。我总是直接说我不感兴趣，每次都会把他们惹火。他们马上会觉得我自私、固执、心眼小；一谈到交易，这些我全都占，恐怕还远不止。让你赚钱的那些技能，在圈外人看来通常都是毛病。我为什么不再读关于交易的书或文章，也不再和别的交易者聊他们的想法？我说过了，图会告诉我一切我需要知道的东西，其他任何信息都是干扰。有几个人被我这个态度冒犯过，但我认为部分原因是我拒绝了他们那些看似对我有帮助的东西，而实际上他们是在做一种奉献，希望我回赠一些指导。我告诉他们我不想听任何人的交易技术时，他们就变得又沮丧又生气。我告诉他们，我连自己那套都还没掌握，可能永远也掌握不了，但我确信，把已经会的东西磨到精，赚的钱会远多于把非价格行为的方法掺进我的交易。我问他们：假如詹姆斯·高威把一支漂亮的长笛送给马友友，并坚持说马友友应该开始学长笛，因为高威吹长笛赚了那么多钱，马友友应该接受吗？显然不该。马友友应该继续在大提琴上越拉越好，这样做他赚的钱会远多于顺带再去学长笛。我既不是高威也不是马友友，但道理是一样的。价格行为是唯一一件我想演奏的乐器，我坚信，精通它赚到的钱会远多于把其他成功交易者的想法掺进来。


> Friends and colleagues freely offer opinions for you to ignore. Occasionally traders will tell me that they have a great setup and want to discuss it with me. I invariably get them angry at me when I tell them that I am not interested. They immediately perceive me as selfish, stubborn, and close-minded, and when it comes to trading, I am all of that and probably much more. The skills that make you money are generally seen as flaws to the lay person. Why do I no longer read books or articles about trading, or talk to other traders about their ideas? As I said, the chart tells me all that I need to know, and any other information is a distraction. Several people have been offended by my attitude, but I think it in part comes from me turning down what they are presenting as something helpful to me when in reality they are making an offering, hoping that I will reciprocate with some tutoring. They become frustrated and angry when I tell them that I don't want to hear about anyone else's trading techniques. I tell them that I haven't even mastered my own and probably never will, but I am confident that I will make far more money perfecting what I already know than trying to incorporate non-price action approaches into my trading. I ask them if James Galway offered a beautiful flute to Yo Yo Mah and insisted that Yo Yo start learning the flute because Galway makes so much money by playing his flute, should Mah accept the offer? Clearly not. Mah should continue to become better and better at the cello and by doing so he will make far more money than if he also started playing the flute. I am no Galway or Mah, but the concept is the same. Price action is the only instrument that I want to play and I strongly believe that I will make far more money by mastering it than by incorporating ideas from other successful traders.


昨天，好市多（Costco）的季度盈利上涨了32%，高于分析师的预期。它开盘跳空高开后，在第一根K线上测试了这个缺口，随后二十分钟里涨了一美元多。（见图 P.2。）之后它又缓慢下探，测试昨天的收盘价。它有两波上涨行情都突破了空头趋势线，两波都失败了。由此形成了双顶（第2根和第3根K线）熊旗，或者叫三顶（第1、第2和第3根K线），随后市场暴跌三美元，跌破了前一日低点。如果你完全不知道那份财报，你会在第2根和第3根K线的空头趋势线突破失败处做空，还会在第4根K线的突破回调处加码做空。你会在第5根K线——一根巨大的反转K线——上反手做多，那是向下突破昨日低点的第二次反转尝试，也是对陡峭空头趋势通道线下沿之突破的高潮反转。换个做法，你本来可能因为那份利多财报而在开盘买入，然后满心焦虑：这只股票为什么在暴跌，而不是像电视上的分析师预测的那样一飞冲天，结果你可能在第5根K线那一轮二次急跌中卖掉了自己的多头仓位。


> Yesterday, Costco's earnings were up 32 percent on the quarter and above analysts' expectations. It gapped up on the open, tested the gap on the first bar and then ran up over a dollar in twenty minutes. (See Figure P.2.) It then drifted down to test yesterday's close. It had two rallies that broke bear trendlines, and both failed. This created a Double Top (Bars 2 and 3) Bear Flag or Triple Top (Bars 1, 2, and 3) and the market then plunged three dollars, below the prior day's low. If you were unaware of the report, you would have shorted at the failed bear trendline breaks at Bars 2 and 3 and you would have sold more on the Breakout Pullback at Bar 4. You would have reversed to long on the Bar 5 big reversal bar, which was the second attempt to reverse the breakout below yesterday's low and a climactic reversal of the breakout of the bottom of the steep bear trend channel line. Alternatively, you could have bought the open because of the bullish report, and then worried about why the stock was collapsing instead of soaring the way that TV analysts predicted, and you likely would have sold out your long on the second plunge down to Bar 5.


任何在极少数几根K线里走完很多点的趋势——也就是说，它是大K线与彼此很少重叠的K线之间的某种组合——最终都会有回调。这类趋势动量极强，所以概率偏向于回调之后去测试趋势的极端点，而且只要回调没有变成新趋势、没有延伸越过先前趋势的起点，极端点通常会被越过。一般来说，如果回调回撤了75% 或更多，回调重新回到先前趋势极端点的概率就会大幅下降。空头趋势里出现这样的回调时，交易者此时最好把这次回调当成一个新的多头趋势，而不是老空头趋势中的一次回调。第6根K线大约是一次70% 的回调，随后市场在第二天开盘时测试了那次高潮式的空头低点。


> Any trend that covers a lot of points in very few bars, meaning that there is some combination of large bars and bars with very little overlap, will eventually have a pullback. These trends have such strong momentum that the odds favor a test of the trend's extreme after the pullback and usually the extreme will be exceeded, as long as the pullback does not become a new trend and extend beyond the start of the prior trend. In general, the odds that a pullback will get back to the prior trend's extreme fall substantially if the pullback retraces 75 percent or more. For a pullback in a bear, at that point, a trader is better to think of the pullback as a new bull trend rather than a pullback in an old bear. Bar 6 was about a 70 percent pullback and then the market tested the climactic bear low on the open of the next day.


**图 P.2　你是该依据一份出色的财报去买，还是依据价格行为去做空？**


唯一和它看上去一样的东西，就是图表本身。如果你弄不清它在告诉你什么，就别交易。等清晰。它总会到来。但一旦它来了，你就必须下单，承担风险，按你的计划走。不要缩小到1分钟图上去把止损收紧，因为你会亏钱。1分钟图的问题是，它用大量的入场机会来诱惑你。可你不可能把它们全吃下，于是你会挑挑拣拣，而这会要了你账户的命；你挑中的坏果子往往太多。最好的那些交易往往快得让你来不及下单，这意味着你只能在那些不那么理想的交易里挑，亏损也就更频繁。当你按5分钟图入场时，你的交易依据是你对5分钟图的分析，而你对1分钟图是什么样一无所知。因此你必须依赖你5分钟图上的止损和目标，并且接受这个现实：1分钟图会朝对你不利的方向走，还会频繁打掉1分钟图上的止损。如果你盯着1分钟图看，你就不会把全部注意力放在5分钟图上，我就会把你账户里的钱拿到我账户里来。想参与竞争，你就必须把所有干扰、把所有除眼前这张图之外的信息输入都减到最少，并且相信：只要做到了，你就会赚到很多钱。这看起来会很不真实，但它非常真实。绝不要怀疑它。把事情保持简单，遵循你简单的规则。始终如一地做一件简单的事极其困难，但在我看来，这是最佳交易方式。最终，随着交易者越来越懂价格行为，交易会变得压力小得多，实际上还挺无聊，但赚钱多得多。


> The only thing that is as it seems is the chart. If you cannot figure out what it is telling you, do not trade. Wait for clarity. It will always come. But once it is there, you must place the trade and assume the risk and follow your plan. Do not dial down to a 1-minute chart and tighten your stop because you will lose. The problem with the 1-minute chart is that it tempts you by offering lots of entries. However, you will not be able to take them all and you will instead cherry-pick, which will lead to the death of your account; you will invariably pick too many bad cherries. The best trades often happen too fast for you to place your orders and that means you will be choosing among the less desirable trades and will lose more often. When you enter on a 5-minute chart, your trade is based on your analysis of the 5-minute chart without any idea of what the 1-minute looks like. You must therefore rely on your 5-minute stops and targets, and just accept the reality that the 1-minute chart will move against you and hit a 1-minute stop frequently. If you watch the 1-minute chart, you will not be devoting your full attention to the 5-minute chart and I will take your money from your account and put it in my account. If you want to compete, you must minimize all distractions and all inputs other than what is on the chart in front of you, and trust that if you do, you will make a lot of money. It will seem unreal but it is very real. Never question it. Just keep things simple and follow your simple rules. It is extremely difficult to consistently do something simple, but in my opinion, it is the best way to trade. Ultimately, as a trader understands price action better and better, trading becomes much less stressful and actually pretty boring, but much more profitable.


虽然我从不赌博，因为概率对我不利，我也从不想和数学对赌，但交易与赌博确有一些相似之处，尤其是在那些不做交易的人的头脑里。比如，有些交易者使用简单的博弈论，在连续一次或多次亏损之后加大交易规模。二十一点里数牌的赌客就和交易区间的交易者非常相似。数牌客想判断的是，什么时候数学已经朝一个方向偏得太远了。具体说，他想知道什么时候牌堆里剩下的牌很可能被花牌压得过重。当他的计数显示这很可能时，他就依据花牌出现比例偏高的概率下一注（赌一把），以提高自己赢的机会。交易区间的交易者则在寻找这样的时刻：他认为市场已经朝一个方向走得太远，然后朝相反方向下单（反向操作）。


> Although I never gamble because the odds are against me and I never want to bet against math, there are some similarities with gambling, especially in the minds of those who don't trade. For example, some traders use simple game theory and increase the size of a trade after one or more losing trades. Blackjack card counters are very similar to trading range traders. The card counter is trying to determine when the math has gone too far in one direction. In particular, he wants to know then the remaining cards in the deck are likely overweighed with face cards. When his count indicates that this is likely, he places a trade (bet) based on the probability that a disproportionate number of face cards will be coming up, increasing his odds of winning. A trading range trader is looking for times when he thinks the market has gone too far in one direction and then he places his trade in the opposite direction (a fade).


一个不幸的事实是，交易的某些方面与赌博非常相似——其中最重要的一点是，许多亏钱的玩法赢的次数足够多，多到让你相信你终究能找到办法长期战胜它。你是在对抗无情的、不可阻挡的数学，想打败它只会把你打到破产。最明显的例子就是按1分钟图交易。既然它看起来和5分钟图一样，既然靠它日内交易能做出很多盈利交易，那么把它当作你的主图，逻辑上似乎说得通。然而，最佳交易中有太多快得根本抓不住，你最后手里只剩二流的交易。随着时间推移，你要么破产，要么比按5分钟图交易赚得少得多。


> One unfortunate reality is that there are aspects of trading that are very similar to gambling-the most important one is that many losing games win often enough to make you believe that you will be able to find a way to win at them in the long run. You are fighting relentless, unstoppable math and you will go broke trying to beat it. The most obvious example is trading off the 1-minute chart. Since it looks the same as the 5-minute and since you can make many winning trades day trading it, it is logical to conclude that you can use it as your primary chart. However, too many of the best trades happen too fast to catch and you will find yourself left with the second-tier trades. Over time, you will either go broke or make substantially less than you would off the 5-minute chart.


还有一种不幸的类比，来自不做交易的人：他们认定所有的日内交易者——其实所有的市场交易者——都是赌瘾缠身的病人。我猜其中确实有不少人是这样：他们做交易更多是为刺激而不是为利润，愿意下低概率的注、亏掉大笔的钱，就为了偶尔赢一把时那股巨大的兴奋。然而，大多数成功的交易者本质上都是投资者，就跟买商业地产或买下一家小生意的投资者一样。与其他任何类型的投资相比，真正不同的只有两点：时间级别更短，杠杆更大。


> One unfortunate comparison is from non-traders who assume that all day traders, and all market traders for that matter, are addicted gamblers and therefore have a mental illness. I suspect that many are in that they are doing it more for excitement than for profit and are willing to make low probability bets and lose large sums of money because of the huge rush they feel when they occasionally win. However, most successful traders are essentially investors, just like an investor who buys commercial real estate or a small business. The only real differences from any other type of investing are that the time frame is shorter and the leverage is greater.


关于赌博还有最后一点。蒙特卡洛方法在理论上很好用，在实践中却不管用，因为数学与情绪会起冲突。如果你每次亏损都把仓位规模翻倍（甚至翻三倍）并反手，理论上你会赚钱。虽然在 Emini 的5分钟图上连续四次亏损很罕见（尤其当你避开在当天区间中部的窄幅横盘交易区间里交易时），但它们还是会出现，六次、七次甚至更多次也会出现，尽管我记不得自己见过。无论如何，如果你做十个合约觉得舒服，又决定每亏一次就翻倍反手，但却从一个合约开始，那么连续四次亏损就需要十六个合约，而在四次亏损之后，你不太可能下出一笔比你舒适区更大的单。再说，如果你喜欢做十个合约，你也不会满足于做一个合约的利润——可那恰恰是你大多数时候最终会做的规模。


> One final point about gambling. Monte Carlo techniques work well in theory but not in practice because of the conflict between math and emotion. If you double (or even triple) your position size and reverse at each loss, you will theoretically make money. Although four losers in a row is rare on the 5-minute Emini chart (especially if you avoid trading in small sideways trading ranges in the middle of the day's range), they will happen, and so will six, seven, or more, even though I can't remember ever seeing that. In any case, if you are comfortable trading ten contracts and you decide to double and reverse with each loser, but begin with one contract, four consecutive losers would require sixteen contracts and it is unlikely that you would place a trade that is larger than your comfort zone following four losers. Also, if you like trading ten contracts, you will not be satisfied with the profit from trading one contract, which is what you would end up trading most of the time.


普通人还担心崩盘的风险，而正因为有这种风险，他们又一次把交易和赌博联系起来。崩盘在日线图上非常罕见（但在日内图上很常见）。他们害怕的是自己在极度情绪化的事件中丧失正常发挥的能力。虽然“崩盘”这个词一般只留给日线图，用来指短时间内发生的、约20% 或以上的空头市场，比如1927年和1987年，但把它只当作一个简单而常见的图形来看待更有用，因为这样就去掉了情绪，帮助交易者遵循自己的规则。如果你把一张图的时间和价格坐标轴去掉，只看价格行为，那么日内图上发生的一些市场走势，与经典崩盘里的形态根本无法区分。如果你能闯过情绪这一关，你就能从崩盘中赚到钱，因为和所有图表一样，它们展示的是可交易的价格行为。


> Lay people are also concerned about the risk of crashes and because of that risk, they again associate trading with gambling. Crashes are very rare on daily charts (but common on intraday charts). They are afraid of their inability to function effectively during extremely emotional events. Although the term "crash" is generally reserved for daily charts and applied to bear markets of about 20 percent or more happening in a short time frame, like in 1927 and 1987, it is more useful to think of it as just a simple and common chart pattern because that removes the emotion and helps a trader follow his rules. If you remove the time and price axes from a chart and focus simply on the price action, there are market movements that occur on intraday charts that are indistinguishable from the patterns in a classic crash. If you can get passed the emotion, you can make money off crashes because with all charts, they display tradable price action.


图 P.3（来自 TradeStation）展示了市场如何在任何时间级别上崩盘。左边那张是1987年崩盘期间 GE 的日线图，中间是 COST 在一份非常强劲的财报之后的5分钟图，右边是一张 Emini 的1分钟图。虽然“崩盘”一词几乎专指日线图上短时间内的20% 或以上抛售，在过去一百年里也被广泛使用过两次，但价格行为交易者看的是形状，而同样的崩盘形态在日内图上很常见。既然崩盘在日内如此常见，这个词也就没有必要用了，因为从交易的角度看，它们只是一段价格行为可交易的下跌行情。


> Figure P.3 (from TradeStation) shows how markets can crash in any timeframe. The one on the left is a daily chart of GE during the 1987 crash, the middle is a 5-minute chart of COST after a very strong earnings report, and the one on the right is a 1-minute Emini chart. Although the term "crash" is used almost exclusively to refer to a 20 percent or more selloff over a short time on a daily chart and was widely used only twice in past hundred years, a price action trader looks for shape and the same crash pattern is common on intraday charts. Since crashes are so common intraday, there is no need to apply the term because from a trading perspective, they are just a bear swing with tradable price action.


大多数交易者只在做背离和趋势回调时才考虑价格行为。他们喜欢看到大反转K线收得很强，但实际上这种情况相当罕见。理解价格行为最有用的工具是趋势线和趋势通道线、先前的高点与低点、突破与突破失败、蜡烛实体和影线的大小，以及当前K线与先前几根K线之间的关系。


> Most traders only consider price action when trading divergences and trend pullbacks. They like to see a strong close on a large reversal bar, but in reality this is a fairly rare occurrence. The most useful tools for understanding price action are trendlines and trend channel lines, prior highs and lows, breakouts and failed breakouts, the size of bodies and tails on candles, and relationships between the current bar to the prior several bars.


**图 P.3　所有时间级别上的崩盘看起来都一样**


尤其是当前K线的开盘、最高、最低和收盘与先前几根K线的走势相比如何，这能透露很多关于接下来会发生什么的信息。本书中的大多数观察都直接与下单有关，但也有少数只是关于价格行为一些有趣而简单的倾向，它们不够可靠，不足以构成一笔交易的依据。


> In particular, how the open, high, low, and close of the current bar compare to the action of the prior several bars tells a lot about what will happen next. Most of the observations in this book are directly related to placing trades, but a few have to do with simple curious price action tendencies without sufficient dependability to be the basis for a trade.


我个人做 Emini 交易时主要靠蜡烛图，做股票交易时主要靠K线图，但大多数信号在任何类型的图上都看得见，许多甚至在简单的线图上都显而易见。我会主要用5分钟蜡烛图来讲解基本原理，但也会把日线图和周线图讲透。此外，我每天都会在几只股票上做几笔日内波段交易，偶尔依据日线图买入期权，我也会讨论单靠价格行为如何成为这类交易的基础。


> I personally rely mainly on candle charts for Emini trading and bar charts for stock trading, but most signals are also visible on any type of chart and many are even evident on simple line charts. I will focus primarily on 5-minute candle charts to illustrate basic principles but will also thoroughly discuss daily and weekly charts as well. Additionally, I place intraday swing trades on several stocks each day and make occasional option purchases based on daily charts, and will discuss how using price action alone can be the basis for this type of trading.


书里大多数图都演示了许多不同的概念，我在其中大多数图上都标出了关键的价格行为观察点。正因如此，几乎任何一张图都可以放在任何一页上，但我把它们放到了我认为最能说明某个要点的那一节。许多图引用了书中后面才描述的建仓形态，但当它们是重要建仓形态的清晰例子时，我会把它们指出来，这对读第二遍应该有帮助。另外，你白天看到的几乎每一个形态，都可以归入本书的好几个类别。不要浪费时间判断一个反转正在展开为双底回调、还是急速行情与交易区间的低点、还是简单的一个更高的低点。你是交易者，不是档案管理员。当你看到一个反转形态时，直接做这笔交易，别费劲去琢磨哪个名字最贴切。还有，各章并非生来平等。有些对你的成功必不可少，另一些收进来是为了完整。如果你是初学者，重点看第15章，因为它讲的是最佳交易，然后再回头翻前面相关的章节去学更多。不要在“磁力位”和“等距运动”这类概念上花太多时间，因为钱不在那儿。它们被收进来只是因为它们展示了价格行为的某些方面，但并不能提供可靠的交易形态。所有图表都是用 TradeStation 做的。


> Most of the charts in the book demonstrate many different concepts and I indicated key price action observations on most. Because of this, almost any chart could be on any page, but I placed them in the section where I thought they best illustrated a point. Many charts reference setups that are described later in the book, but when they are clear examples of important setups, I point them out, which should be helpful on a second read through the book. Also, almost every pattern that you see during the day can be placed into several categories in this book. Don't waste time deciding if a reversal is unfolding as a Double Bottom Pullback or a Spike and Trading Range low or a simple Higher Low. You are a trader, not a file clerk. When you see a reversal pattern, just take the trade and don't labor over which name most accurately applies. Also, not all chapters are created equal. Some are essential to your success whereas others are included for completeness. If you are a beginner, focus on Chapter 15 because it describes the best trades, and then refer back to the appropriate earlier chapters to learn more. Don't spend a lot of time on concepts like Magnets and Measured Moves, because that is not where the money is. They are included simply because they demonstrate aspects of price action, but do not offer reliable trading patterns. All of the charts were created with TradeStation.


因为我在加利福尼亚做交易，所有图表用的都是太平洋标准时间。


> Since I trade in California, all of the charts are in Pacific Standard Time.


# 第 1 章　价格行为

*Chapter 1. Price Action*


对交易者来说，一天之中反复面对的根本问题，就是判断市场到底有没有趋势。如果市场有趋势，他就假定这个趋势会延续，并顺着趋势的方向寻找入场机会（“顺势”）。如果市场没有趋势，他就会在最近那段行情的反方向上寻找入场机会（“反向操作”或“逆势”）。趋势可以短到只有一根K线（在更小的时间级别上，这根K线内部也可以包含一段强趋势），而在5分钟图上，它也可以持续一天甚至更久。他凭什么做这个判断？靠读懂眼前这张图上的价格行为。


> For a trader, the fundamental issue that confronts him repeatedly throughout the day is the decision of whether the market is trending or not trending. If it is trending, he assumes that the trend will continue, and he will look to enter in the direction of the trend ("With Trend"). If it is not trending, he will look to enter in the opposite direction of the most recent move ("fade" or "Countertrend"). A trend can be as short as a single bar (on a smaller time frame, there can be a strong trend contained within that bar) or, on a 5-minute chart, it can last a day or more. How does he make this decision? By reading the price action on the chart in front of him.


对交易者来说，价格行为最有用的定义也是最简单的：它就是任何走势图类型、任何时间级别上的任何价格变化。变化的最小单位是 tick（最小报价单位），每个市场里它代表的价值都不一样。顺带说一句，tick 有两个含义：一是市场能够给出的最小价格变动单位，二是每一笔实际发生的成交（所以如果你买入，你的委托会出现在成交明细表上，而你这一笔成交不论大小，都算一个 tick）。由于盘中价格随着每一个 tick（每一笔成交）而变化，每一次价格变化都成了价格行为的一个例子。价格行为没有一个公认的定义；既然你始终要努力去留意市场给出的每一条信息、哪怕它看起来最不重要，你的定义就必须非常宽泛。你不能忽略任何东西，因为起初看起来微不足道的信号，往往就会引出一笔好交易。最宽泛的定义涵盖交易过程中价格运动的任何表现形式，它包含任何金融品种、任何走势图类型、任何时间级别。


> The most useful definition of price action for a trader is also the simplest: it is any change in price on any chart type or time frame. The smallest unit of change is the tick, which has a different value for each market. Incidentally, a tick has two meanings. It is the smallest unit of change in price that a market can make, and it is also every trade that takes place (so if you buy, your order will appear on the Time and Sales table, and your fill, no matter how large or small, is one tick). Since price is changing with every tick (trade) during the day, each price change becomes an example of price action. There is no universally accepted definition of price action, and since you need to always try to be aware of even the seemingly least significant piece of information that the market is offering, you must have a very broad definition. You cannot dismiss anything because very often something that initially appears minor leads to a great trade. The broadest definition includes any representation of price movement during the course of trading. This includes any financial instrument, on any type of chart, in any time frame.


光有定义，并不能告诉你该怎么下单，因为每一根K线都既是做空的潜在信号，也是做多的潜在信号。市场上总有人在等着做空下一个 tick，认定市场不会再高一个 tick；也总有人在买入，认定市场多半不会再低一个 tick。总有一方是对的，另一方是错的。如果买方错了，市场低了一个 tick，接着又低一个，再低一个，他们就会开始考虑自己的判断可能出了问题。到了某个时点，他们不得不亏损卖出自己的持仓，于是从买方变成了新的卖方，这又会把市场进一步推低。卖方会持续入场，有的是新开的空头，有的是被迫平仓的多头，直到某个时点更多买方进来为止。这些买方里既有新买家，也有获利平仓的空头，还有现在已经亏损、不得不买入回补持仓的新空头。市场会继续上行，直到同样的过程再次反转。


> The definition alone does not tell you anything about placing a trade because every bar is a potential signal both for a short and a long trade. There are traders out there who will be looking to short the next tick, believing that the market won't go one tick higher, and others who will buy it believing that the market will likely not go one tick lower. One side will be right, and the other will be wrong. If the buyers are wrong and the market goes one tick lower and then another and then another, they will begin to entertain the prospect that their belief is wrong. At some point, they will have to sell their position at a loss, making them new sellers and no longer buyers, and this will drive the market down further. Sellers will continue to enter the market, either as new shorts or as longs forced to liquidate, until some point when more buyers come in. These buyers will be a combination of new buyers, profit-taking shorts, and new shorts who now have a loss and will have to buy to cover their positions. The market will continue up until the process reverses once again.


一切都是相对的，一切都可能在一瞬间变成完全相反的样子，哪怕价格没有任何变动。也许你突然看到，在当前K线高点上方七个 tick 处有一条趋势线，于是你不再想做空，而是想买入，去测试那条趋势线。透过后视镜做交易，是必亏的路子。你必须一直往前看，不要为刚犯的错误烦心——它们对下一个 tick 没有任何影响，所以你必须把它们丢开，只管继续重新评估价格行为，而不是盯着当天的盈亏（P&L）。


> Everything is relative, and everything can change into the exact opposite in an instant, even without any movement in price. It might be that you suddenly see a trendline seven ticks above the high of the current bar and instead of looking to short, you now are looking to buy for a test of the trendline. Trading through the rearview mirror is a sure way to lose money. You have to keep looking ahead, not worrying about the mistakes you just made. They have absolutely no bearing on the next tick, so you must ignore them and just keep reassessing the price action and not your profit and loss (P&L) on the day.


每一个 tick 都会改变每一张时间级别图上的价格行为，从 tick 图、1分钟图一直到月线图，也改变所有走势图上的价格行为，不管这张图是基于时间、成交量、成交笔数、点数图，还是别的什么。显而易见，一个 tick 的变动在月线图上通常没有意义（除非，比如说，它是某个图表价位上一个 tick 的突破、并且立刻反转），但在时间级别越小的图上，它就越有用。道理很明显：如果今天 Emini 小型合约1分钟图上的平均K线高度是三个 tick，那么一个 tick 的变动就相当于平均K线高度的33%，这可能代表一次不小的运动。


> Each tick changes the price action of every time frame chart from a tick chart or 1-minute chart through a monthly chart, and on all charts, whether the chart is based on time, volume, the number of ticks, point and figure, or anything else. Obviously, a single tick move is usually meaningless on a monthly chart (unless, for example, it is a one tick breakout of some chart point that immediately reverses), but it becomes increasingly more useful on smaller time frame charts. This is obviously true because if the average bar today on a 1-minute Emini chart is three ticks tall, then a one tick move is 33 percent of the size of the average bar, and that can represent a significant move.


价格行为最有用的地方，是观察市场越过（突破）图上此前的K线或趋势线之后发生了什么。举例来说，如果市场涨过了一个重要的前期高点，并且之后的每一根K线都形成比前一根K线更高的低点和更高的高点，那么这种价格行为表明，市场在后续某一根K线上很可能会更高，哪怕近期它会回调几根K线。反过来，如果市场向上突破，接着下一根K线是一根小的内包K线（它的高点不高于那根大突破K线的高点），再下一根K线的低点又低于这根小K线，那么突破失败、反转回落的概率就会大幅上升。


> The most useful aspect of price action is watching what happens after the market moves beyond (breaks out beyond) prior bars or trendlines on the chart. For example, if the market goes above a significant prior high and each subsequent bar forms a low that is above the prior bar's low and a high that is above the prior bar's high, then this price action indicates that the market will likely be higher on some subsequent bar, even if it pulls back for a few bars near term. On the other hand, if the market breaks out to the upside, and then the next bar is a small inside bar (its high is not higher than that of the large breakout bar), and then the following bar has a low that is below this small bar, the odds of a failed breakout and a reversal back down increase considerably.


长期来看，基本面决定一只股票的价格，而这个价格是由机构交易者（共同基金、银行、券商、保险公司、养老基金、对冲基金等等）设定的，它们是成交量最大的参与者。价格行为就是机构在寻找价值的过程中沿途留下的运动。当它们觉得价格太高，就会离场甚至做空；当它们觉得价格太低（有价值），就会做多，或者对自己的空头止盈。阴谋论者永远不会相信，但机构确实不会开秘密会议去投票决定价格应该在哪里、好从毫无防备、本意良好的散户手里把钱骗走。它们的投票本质上是独立且保密的，形式就是它们的买卖，而结果展示在价格图上。短期而言，机构可以操纵一只股票的价格，尤其是在成交清淡的品种上。不过，相比它们用其他交易方式能赚到的钱，这么做赚得相对少得多，所以操纵这件事根本不值得担心，尤其是在成交量巨大的股票和市场里，比如 Emini 系列、主要股票、债券工具和外汇。


> Over time, fundamentals control the price of a stock, and that price is set by institutional traders (like mutual funds, banks, brokerage houses, insurance companies, pension funds, hedge funds, and so on), who are by far the biggest volume players. Price action is the movement that takes place along the way as institutions probe for value. When they feel that the price is too high, they will exit or even short, and when they feel it is too low (a good value), they will go long or take profits on their shorts. Although conspiracy theorists will never believe it, institutions do not have secret meetings to vote on what the price should be in an attempt to steal money from unsuspecting, well-intentioned individual traders. Their voting is essentially independent and secret, and comes in the form of their buying and selling, but the results are displayed on price charts. In the short run, an institution can manipulate the price of a stock, especially if it is thinly traded. However, they would make relatively much less money doing that compared to what they could make in other forms of trading, making the concern of manipulation of negligible importance, especially in stocks and markets where huge volume is traded, like the Eminis, major stocks, debt instruments, and currencies.


为什么价格会向上走一个 tick？因为在当前价位上，愿意出价买入的量大于愿意卖出的量，而且这些买家中有不少人愿意在必要时出比当前价更高的价。这种情况有时被描述为市场上的买方多于卖方，或者说买方掌控着局面，或者说存在买压。当所有能够在当前价位（最后成交价）成交的买单都成交完之后，剩下的买家就必须决定，自己是否愿意高一个 tick 买入。如果愿意，他们就会继续在更高的价位出价。这个更高的价格会让所有市场参与者重新评估自己对市场的看法。如果愿意出价买入的量仍然大于愿意卖出的量，价格就会继续上行，因为在最后成交价上，卖方提供的合约数量不足以满足买方的买入需求。到了某个时点，买家会在部分止盈的时候开始挂出部分合约。同时，卖方会认为当前价格是做空的好价位，愿意卖出的量超过买方想买的量。一旦卖方提供的合约（要么是想回补部分或全部多头合约的买家，要么是试图做空的新卖方）变多，所有买单都会在当前价位成交，但一部分卖方找不到足够的买家。买价于是向下走一个 tick。如果有卖方愿意在这个更低的价位卖出，它就成了新的最后成交价。


> Why does price move up one tick? It is because there is more volume being bid at the current price than being offered, and a number of those buyers are willing to pay even more than the current price if necessary. This is sometimes described as the market having more buyers than sellers, or as the buyers being in control, or as buying pressure. Once all of those buy orders that can possibly be filled are filled at the current price (the last price traded), the remaining buyers will have to decide whether they are willing to buy at one tick higher. If they are, they will continue to bid at the higher price. This higher price will make all market participants reevaluate their perspective on the market. If there continues to be more volume being bid than offered, price will continue to move up since there are an insufficient number of contracts being offered by sellers at the last price to fill the requests to buy by buyers. At some point, buyers will start offering some of their contracts as they take partial profits. Also, sellers will perceive the current price as a good value for a short and offer to sell more than buyers want to buy. Once there are more contracts being offered by sellers (either buyers who are looking to cover some or all of their long contracts or by new sellers who are attempting to short), all of the buy orders will be filled at the current price, but some sellers will be unable to find enough buyers. The bid will move down a tick. If there are sellers willing to sell at this lower price, this will become the new last price.


既然大多数市场都是由机构的委托驱动的，那么很自然会想：机构是把价格行为当作入场的依据，还是它们的行动本身在制造价格行为？实际情况是，机构并不是全体都在一个 tick 一个 tick 地盯着 AAPL 或 SPY（标普500的 ETF），看到1分钟图上出现一个两段式回调就启动买入程序。它们一天当中有大量委托要成交，所做的是尽量以最好的价格把它们成交掉。价格行为只是众多考虑因素之一：有些公司更依赖它，另一些公司依赖得少一些，或者根本不看。许多公司有数学模型和程序来决定何时买卖、买卖多少，而所有公司一整天都在不断接到客户的新委托。


> Since most markets are driven by institutional orders, it is reasonable to wonder whether the institutions are basing their entries on price action, or whether their actions are causing the price action. The reality is that institutions are not all watching AAPL or SPY tick by tick and then starting a buy program when they see a two-legged pullback on a 1-minute chart. They have a huge number of orders to be filled during the day and are working to fill them at the best price. Price action is just one of many considerations, and some firms will rely more on it, and others will rely on it less or not at all. Many firms have mathematical models and programs that determine when and how much to buy and sell, and all firms continue to receive new orders from clients all day long.


交易者盘中看到的价格行为，是机构活动的结果，而远不是这种活动的原因。当一个能赚钱的建仓形态展开时，这笔交易的成败会同时受到许多无从知晓的力量影响。建仓形态其实是一段已经在路上的行情的第一个阶段，而价格行为入场只是让交易者早早跳上这波浪。随着更多价格行为展开，更多交易者会顺着行情方向入场，在图上制造动能，又引得更多交易者入场。交易者（包括机构）出于你能想象到的任何理由挂出卖价和买价，而这些理由基本上无关紧要。不过，有一个理由是重要的，因为聪明的价格行为交易者一眼就能看出来——利用被套的交易者获利。如果你知道保护性止损就挂在一根K线下方一个 tick 处、而且会让刚刚买入的人亏钱，那你就应该在同一价位上挂卖出止损单做空，从那些被逼出场的被套者身上赚钱。


> The price action that traders see during the day is the result of institutional activity and much less the cause of the activity. When a profitable setup unfolds, there will be a confluence of unknowable influences taking place during the trade that results in the trade being profitable or a loser. The setup is the actual first phase of a move that is already underway and a price action entry lets a trader just jump onto the wave early on. As more price action unfolds, more traders will enter in the direction of the move, generating momentum on the charts, causing additional traders to enter. Traders, including institutions, place their bids and offers for every imaginable reason, and the reasons are largely irrelevant. However, one reason that is relevant, because it is evident to smart price action traders, is to benefit from trapped traders. If you know that protective stops are located at one tick below a bar and will result in losses to traders who just bought, then you should get short on a stop at that same price to make a profit off the trapped traders as they are forced out.


既然机构活动主导着行情，它们的成交量又如此巨大，而且它们下单时大多打算持有几个小时到几个月，所以大多数机构并不想剥头皮，相反，它们会捍卫自己最初的入场。如果 Vanguard 或 Fidelity 要为旗下的某只共同基金买入股票，它们的客户会希望这只基金在收盘时持有股票。客户买共同基金，不是指望基金去做日内交易、到收盘时全变成现金。基金必须持有股票，也就是说它们必须买入并持有，而不是买入并剥头皮。举例来说，在初次买入之后，它们很可能还有多得多的量要买，于是会利用任何一次小幅回调加仓；如果没有回调，它们就会在市场上涨的过程中继续买入。


> Since institutional activity controls the move and their volume is so huge and they place most of their trades with the intention of holding them for hours to months, most will not be looking to scalp and instead they will defend their original entry. If Vanguard or Fidelity have to buy stock for one of their mutual funds, their clients will want the fund to own stock at the end of the day. Clients do not buy mutual funds with the expectation that the funds will day trade and end up in all cash by the close. The funds have to own stock, which means they have to buy and hold, not buy and scalp. For example, after their initial buy, they will likely have much more to buy and will use any small pullback to add on. If there is none, they will continue to buy as the market rises.


有些新手交易者想不通：市场一路直线上涨的时候，到底是谁在买？他们也不明白，为什么会有人在市价上追着买，而不是等一次回调。答案很简单：是机构在以尽可能好的价格成交它们所有的委托，市场越涨，它们越会拆成很多笔去买。这类交易中有很大一部分是机构的计算机程序在做，程序跑完它就会结束。如果一笔交易失败，更可能的原因是交易者误读了价格行为，而不是某个机构在启动程序几分钟后就改变主意，或者赚了两三个 tick 就落袋。


> Some beginner traders wonder who is buying as the market is going straight up and also wonder why anyone would buy at the market instead of waiting for a pullback. The answer is simple. It is institutions working to fill all of their orders at the best possible price, and they will buy in many pieces as the market continues up. A lot of this trading is being done by institutional computer programs, and it will end after the programs are complete. If a trade fails, it is far more likely the result of the trader misreading the price action than it is of an institution changing its mind or taking a couple ticks of profit within minutes of initiating a program.


意识到机构才是价格行为的主因，其唯一的用处在于：它让依据价格行为下单变得更可靠。大多数机构不会进进出出地做日内交易，不会在你每次入场之后就让市场反转。你的价格行为入场，只是搭机构便车的一笔交易；但与它们不同的是，你是把整笔交易或其中一部分用来剥头皮。


> The only importance of realizing that institutions are responsible for price action is that it makes placing trades based on price action more reliable. Most institutions are not going to be day trading in and out, making the market reverse after every one of your entries. Your price action entry is just a piggyback trade on their activity, but, unlike them, you are scalping all or part of your trade.


确实有些公司会做很大量的日内交易。不过，它们的交易要能赚钱，市场必须顺着它们的方向走出很多个 tick；而价格行为交易者会看到一段行情最早的那部分，从而能早早进场，并有信心认为剥头皮成功的概率很高。如果那家机构只想剥4个或8个 tick，它就不可能让市场逆着自己走15个 tick。因此，只有当它们觉得逆向波动的风险很小时才会入场。如果你能从图上读出它们的活动，你也应该对自己的交易有信心，但始终要在市场里挂一张止损单，以防自己读错。


> There are some firms that day trade substantial volume. However, for their trades to be profitable the market has to move many ticks in their direction, and a price action trader will see the earliest parts of the move, allowing her to get in early and be confident that the odds of a successful scalp are high. That firm cannot have the market go 15 ticks against them if they are trying to scalp 4 or 8 ticks. As such, they will enter only when they feel that the risk of an adverse move is small. If you read their activity on the charts, you should likewise be confident in your trade, but always have a stop in the market in case your read is wrong.


另外，由于入场K线的极值经常会被精准地测试到（精确到一个 tick 都不差），而止损并没有被打掉，所以在那里一定有机构规模的成交量在保护这些止损，而它们这么做正是依据价格行为。在 Emini 的5分钟图上，有些价格行为事件会改变聪明交易者的看法。举例来说，如果一次做多的高2回调失败了，聪明交易者就会假定市场很可能还要走出两段下跌。如果你是机构交易者，并且买入了那个高2，你不会希望它失败，于是会一路加仓买下去，一直买到那条关键保护性止损价位上方一个 tick 处。这家机构正是在用价格行为支撑自己的多头。


> Also, since often the entry bar extreme is tested to the tick and the stops are not run, there must be institutional size volume protecting the stops, and they are doing so based on price action. In the 5-minute Emini, there are certain price action events that change the perspective of smart traders. For example, if a High 2 long pullback fails, smart traders will assume that the market will likely have two more legs down. If you are an institutional trader and you bought that High 2, you do not want it to fail, and you will buy more all the way down to one tick above that key protective stop price. That institution is using price action to support their long.


那些大的行情段基本上挡不住，但细小的价格行为会被一些盯着每一个 tick 的机构交易者微调。有时，一次做多的五个 tick 的失败正在形成，价格老是只摸到第5个 tick，却到不了第6个 tick——只有到了那里，你才能从多单里剥出4个 tick——这时会突然出现一笔250份 Emini 合约的成交，而价格并没有向下走低。总体而言，在今天的 Emini 市场里，凡是超过100份合约的成交都应该视为机构行为。就算那只是一个资金量很大的个人交易者，他多半也具备机构的眼光；既然他的成交量就是机构级别的，他跟机构没有区别。价格既然还停在第5个 tick 上，那笔250份合约的委托几乎可以肯定就是机构在买入。因为如果机构在一个挤满了紧张多头的市场里卖出，市场会迅速下跌。当机构在市场已经上涨5个 tick 的时候开始买入，它们预期的不只是再高1个 tick；通常在一分钟左右的时间里，价格就会冲过6个 tick、并至少再往上摆出好几个 tick。机构是在高位买入的，这说明它们认为市场还会更高，而且很可能在上涨过程中继续买入。另外，既然4个 tick 的剥头皮如此经常奏效，那么很可能存在机构剥头皮，它对当天大多数剥头皮都施加着很大的影响。


> The big legs are essentially unstoppable, but the small price action is fine-tuned by some institutional traders who are watching every tick. Sometimes when there is a 5-tick long failure setting up and the price just keeps hitting 5 ticks but not 6 where you can scalp 4 ticks out of your long, there will suddenly be a trade of 250 Emini contracts, and the price does not tick down. In general, anything over 100 contracts should be considered institutional in today's Emini market. Even if it is just a large individual trader, he likely has the insight of an institution, and since he is trading institutional volume, he is indistinguishable from an institution. Since the price is still hanging at 5 ticks, almost certainly that 250 lot order was an institutional buy. This is because if institutions were selling in a market filled with nervous longs, the market would fall quickly. When the institutions start buying when the market is up 5 ticks, they expect it to go more than just 1 tick higher and usually within a minute or so the price will surge through 6 ticks and swing up for at least many more. The institutions were buying at the high, which means that they think the market will go higher and they will likely buy more as it goes up. Also, since 4-tick scalps work so often, it is likely that there is institutional scalping that exerts a great influence over most scalps during the day.


交易者会密切关注关键时间级别收盘前的最后几秒，尤其是3分钟、5分钟、15分钟和60分钟K线。对成交量K线图上的关键成交量来说也是如此。举例来说，如果许多交易者都在跟踪十年期美国国债期货合约那张“每根K线10,000股”的成交量图，那么当K线快要收盘时（它是在该K线开始以来成交量首次达到10,000股之后的第一笔成交上收盘的，所以K线很少正好是10,000股），可能会出现一阵密集的成交，去影响这根K线最终的样子。某一方可能想展示出一种意愿，让这根K线看起来更偏多或更偏空。用最简单的话说，一根强多头趋势K线意味着多头掌控了这根K线。在强趋势中，很常见的一种情况是：一根反转K线在5分钟K线收盘前的最后几秒里把样子完全反转过来。举例来说，在强空头里，可能出现一个高2做多的建仓形态，配着一根非常强的多头反转K线。接着，在这根K线收盘前还剩5秒时，价格暴跌，K线收在最低点，把许多抢先入场、原本期待一根多头趋势反转K线的多头全部套住。在强趋势中做逆势交易时，务必等信号K线收盘之后再下单，然后只能顺着交易方向、在这根K线之外1个 tick 处用止损单入场（如果你要做多，就在前一根K线的高点上方1个 tick 处挂买入止损单）。


> Traders pay close attention to the seconds before key time frames close, especially 3-, 5-, 15-, and 60-minute bars. This is also true on key volumes for volume bar charts. For example, if many traders follow the 10,000 shares per bar chart for the Ten Year Note futures contract, then when the bar is about to close (it closes on the first trade of any size that results in at least 10,000 shares traded since the start of the bar, so the bar is rarely ever exactly 10,000 shares), there may be a flurry of activity to influence the final appearance of the bar. One side might want to demonstrate a willingness to make the bar appear more bullish or bearish. In simplest terms, a strong bull trend bar means that the bulls owned the bar. It is very common in strong trends for a reversal bar to totally reverse its appearance in the final few seconds before a 5-minute bar closes. For example, in a strong bear, there might be a High 2 long setting up with a very strong bull reversal bar. Then, with 5 seconds remaining before the bar closes, the price plummets, and the bar closes on its low, trapping lots of front running longs who expected a bull trend reversal bar. When trading Countertrend against a strong trend, it is imperative to wait for the signal bar to close before you place your order, and then only enter on a stop at 1 tick beyond the bar in the direction of your trade (if you are buying, buy at 1 tick above the high of the prior bar on a stop).


学习读价格行为，最好的办法是什么？把图打印出来，然后找出每一笔能赚钱的交易。如果你是剥头皮交易者，想在5分钟图上从 AAPL 上赚50美分、或者从 GOOG 上赚 $2，那就把当天每一次有可能赚到这么多利润的行情都找出来。几周之后，你会开始看出几种形态，它们能让你在这些行情里交易，同时承担大致相当的风险。如果风险与回报相当，你必须赢下远超50% 的次数，这笔交易才划算。不过，很多形态的成功率能达到70% 甚至更高，而且很多交易允许你在等待止盈目标兑现的过程中，把止损从信号K线的极值之外移到入场K线的极值之外，从而降低风险。另外，你应该努力去做那些有机会远远越过止盈目标的交易，因此你只应该分批止盈。事实上，一开始你就该只专注这类入场：把止损移到保本，然后让剩下的仓位继续跑。你很可能每周至少有几笔交易，在形成反向入场形态之前，能跑到初始目标的四倍甚至更多。


> What is the best way to learn how to read price action? It is to print out charts and then look for every profitable trade. If you are a scalper looking for 50 cents in AAPL or $2 in GOOG on the 5-minute chart, then find every move during the day where that amount of profit was possible. After several weeks, you will begin to see a few patterns that would allow you to make those trades while risking about the same amount. If the risk is the same as the reward, you have to win much more than 50 percent of the time to make the trade worthwhile. However, lots of patterns have a 70 percent or better success rate, and many trades allow you to move up your stop from below the signal bar extreme to below the entry bar extreme while waiting for your profit target to be reached, reducing your risk. Also, you should be trying to enter trades that have a good chance of running well past your profit target, and you should therefore only take partial profits. In fact, initially you should only focus on those entries. Move your stop to breakeven and then let the remainder run. You will likely have at least a couple of trades each week that run .to four or more times your initial target before setting up a reverse entry pattern.


斐波那契回撤与扩展是价格行为的一部分，但由于它们大多只是近似值、而且大多都会失败，不要用它们来做交易。如果其中某一个真的有用，它一定会对应着某种本身就可靠、可交易的图形形态，与斐波那契测量或任何指标无关。艾略特波浪理论也是一种价格行为分析，但对大多数交易者来说它并不可交易。通常要等理想入场点之后过了很多很多根K线，浪形才会变清楚；而且在每一个瞬间都存在如此多互相矛盾的解释，对大多数活跃的日内交易者来说，它需要思考的东西太多、不确定性太大。


> Fibonacci retracements and extensions are a part of price action, but since most are just approximations and most fail, do not use them for trading. If one is good, it will be associated with a chart pattern that is reliable and tradable on its own, independent of the Fibonacci measurement or any indicators. Elliott Wave Theory is also a type of price action analysis, but for most traders it is not tradable. The waves are usually not clear until many, many bars after the ideal entry point, and with so many opposite interpretations at every instant, it requires far too much thought and uncertainty for most active day traders.


你是否该担心：把这本书里的信息公开之后，会造就一大批优秀的价格行为交易者，他们全都在同一时间做同一件事，于是再也没有后来者进场，把市场推到你的止盈目标？不会。因为市场由机构掌控，而它们已经拥有世界上最聪明的交易者，这些交易者早就知道这本书里的一切，至少是凭直觉知道。我们大家看到的形态之所以是那个样子，是因为这就是一个有效市场里出现的样子：无数交易者出于成千上万种不同的理由下单，而真正主导的成交量是依据合理的逻辑成交的。它看起来就是这个样子，而且一直如此。同样的形态在全世界所有市场的所有时间级别上都会出现，要让这么多不同层面上的东西同时被操纵，根本不可能。


> Should you be concerned that making the information in this book available will create lots of great price action traders, all doing the same thing at the same time, thereby removing the late entrants needed to drive the market to your price target? No, because the institutions control the market, and they already have the smartest traders in the world, and those traders already know everything in this book, at least intuitively. The reason that the patterns that we all see unfold as they do is because that is the appearance that occurs in an efficient market with countless traders placing orders for thousands of different reasons, but with the controlling volume being traded based on sound logic. That is just what it looks like, and it has forever. The same patterns unfold on all time frames in all markets around the world and it would simply be impossible for all of it to be manipulated instantaneously on so many different levels.


如果所有人突然都变成价格行为的剥头皮交易者，那些较小的形态在短时间里可能会有点变化；但时间一长，有效市场仍然会胜出，所有交易者的投票会被浓缩成标准的价格行为形态，因为这是无数人按逻辑行事必然产生的结果。而且现实情况是，交易非常难；虽然依据价格行为做交易是一种合理的方法，但要在实时行情里做到，依然非常困难。根本不会有足够多的人、在同一时间、都做得足够好，以致长期对形态产生任何显著影响。看看 Edwards 和 Magee 就知道了：世界上最优秀的交易者已经用了他们的理念几十年，而这些理念依然管用，原因还是同一个……图之所以长成那个样子，是因为那是一个有效市场不可更改的指纹——这个市场里挤满了数量庞大、使用着数量庞大的方法和时间级别的聪明人，所有人都在尽力赚到最多的钱。市场要么在你眼前的图上处于趋势之中，要么不是。当它没有趋势时，它就处在某种交易区间里，而交易区间是由更小时间级别上的趋势构成的。落到单根K线的层面上，它要么是一根趋势K线，要么是一根交易区间K线。要么多头、要么空头在掌控这根K线，要么双方大体处于均衡状态（一根K线构成的交易区间）。


> If everyone suddenly became a price action scalper, the smaller patterns might change a little for a while, but over time, the efficient market action patterns because that is the inescapable result of countless people will win out, and the votes by all traders will get distilled into standard price behaving logically. Also, the reality is that it is very difficult to trade, and although basing trades on price action is a sound approach, it is still very difficult to do real time. There just won't be enough traders doing it well enough, all at the same time, to have any significant influence over time on the patterns. Just look at Edwards and Magee. The best traders in the world have been using those ideas for decades and they continue to work, again for the same reason . . . charts look they way they do because that is the unchangeable fingerprint of an efficient market filled with a huge number of smart people using a huge number of approaches and time frames, all trying to make the most money that they can. The market is either trending on the chart in front of you, or it is not. When it is not, it is in some kind of trading range, which is composed of trends on smaller time frames. On the level of an individual bar, it is either a trend bar or a trading range bar. Either the bulls or bears are in control of the bar, or they are largely in equilibrium (a one bar trading range).


对交易者来说，最有用的是把所有K线都看成两类：趋势K线，或者非趋势（交易区间）K线。后一个叫法有些别扭，而且这类K线大多与十字星相似，所以更简单的做法是：把所有非趋势K线都叫作十字星（十字星K线）（见图 1.1）。如果图上实体显得很小或者根本没有实体，这根K线就是十字星，多空双方都没有掌控它，它本质上就是一根K线构成的交易区间。在 Emini 的5分钟图上，十字星的实体只有一两个 tick 大。但是，在谷歌的日线图或周线图上，实体可能有100个 tick（$1）甚至更大，却仍然与一颗完美的十字星具有同样的含义，因此把它叫作十字星是合理的。这个判断是相对的、主观的，取决于市场和级别。


> For a trader, it is most useful to think of all bars as being either trend bars or nontrend (trading range) bars. Since the latter is an awkward term and most are similar to dojis, it is simpler to refer to all nontrend bars as dojis (doji bars) (see Figure 1. 1). If the body appears tiny or nonexistent on the chart, the bar is a doji, and neither the bulls nor bears controlled the bar, and the bar is essentially a one bar trading range. On a 5-minute Emini chart, a doji body is only a tick or two large. However, on a daily or weekly Google chart, the body can be 100 ticks ($1) or more and still have the same significance as a perfect doji, and therefore it makes sense to refer to it as a doji. The determination is relative and subjective, and it depends on the market and the time frame.


如果存在实体，就说明收盘价相对开盘价走出了趋势，这根K线就是趋势K线。显然，如果K线很大而实体很小，说明趋势的力量不强。另外，在这根K线内部（从更小级别上看）可能有过几段基本横盘的波段，但这无关紧要，因为你只应该盯着一张图。实体越大，通常说明力量越强；但在一段长时间的行情或一次突破之后出现极其巨大的实体，可能代表趋势走到了衰竭的尽头，这时在更多价格行为展开之前不该做任何交易。一连串强趋势K线是趋势健康的标志，后面通常还会出现一个新的极值，哪怕紧接着就发生回调。


> If there is a body, then the close trended away from the open, and the bar is a trend bar. Obviously, if the bar is large and the body is small, there was not much trending strength. Also, within the bar (as seen on a smaller time frame), there may have been several swings of largely sideways movement, but this is irrelevant because you should focus on only one chart. Larger bodies in general indicate more strength, but an extremely large body after a protracted move or a breakout can represent an exhaustive end of a trend, and no trade should be taken until more price action unfolds. A series of strong trend bars is the sign of a healthy trend and will usually be followed by a further extreme, even if a pullback immediately ensues.


理想的趋势K线，实体大小适中，说明到K线收盘时，市场已经相对这根K线的开盘价走出了趋势。最低的要求是：多头趋势K线的收盘价高于开盘价，本书中用白色蜡烛线实体表示。多头可以展示出更强的掌控力的方式，是让实体大约等于甚至大于过去5根或10根K线实体尺寸的中位数。其他强势迹象还包括：开盘价就在低点或接近低点，收盘价在高点或接近高点，收盘价位于此前几根K线的收盘价和高点之上或与之持平，高点高于此前一根或多根K线的高点，以及影线很短。如果这根K线非常大，它可能代表衰竭，或者一次单根K线的假突破——它把新进的多头套住，然后就在接下来的一两根K线里反转下跌。空头趋势K线则相反。


> An ideal trend bar is one with a moderate-size body, indicating that the market trended away from the open of the bar by the time the bar closed. The minimum is a close above the open in a bull trend bar, indicated by a white candle body in this book. The bulls can demonstrate stronger control by having the body be about the size or larger than that of the median body size over the past 5 or 10 bars. Additional signs of strength include the open being on or near the low, the close on or near the high, the close at or above the closes and highs of several prior bars, the high above the high of one or more prior bars, and the tails being small. If the bar is very large, it might represent exhaustion or a one bar false breakout that is trapping new bulls, only to reverse down in the next bar or two. The opposite is true for bear trend bars.


![图 1.1](figures/fig-01-01.png)


**图 1.1　十字星示例**


一切都是相对的，需要不断重新评估，甚至要到彻底改变自己对市场方向的看法那种程度。没错，每一根K线要么是趋势K线，要么是十字星K线，而十字星K线意味着多空双方处于平衡。不过，有时一连串十字星反而可能意味着趋势正在起作用。举例来说，如果出现一连串十字星，每一根的收盘价都比前一根高，其中大多数的高点高于前一根K线的高点、低点高于前一根K线的低点，那么市场正在呈现收盘价、高点、低点的趋势，也就是说趋势正在起作用（见图 1.2）。


> Everything is relative and subject to constant reassessment even to the point of totally changing your opinion about the direction of the market. Yes, every bar is either a trend bar or a doji bar, and a doji bar means that the bulls and bears are in balance. However, sometimes a series of dojis can mean that a trend is in effect. For example, if there is a series of dojis, each with a higher close and most with a high above the high of the prior bar and a low above the low of the prior bar, the market is displaying trending closes, highs, and lows, so a trend is in effect (see Figure 1.2).


从交易的角度看，把所有K线都当成趋势K线或十字星（也就是非趋势K线，图 1.1中用“D”标出）来想是有用的，而这种贴标签的方式本来就不严谨。一根实体很小的K线，在某个价格行为的位置上可能是十字星，换到另一处就是一根小的趋势K线。区分两者的唯一目的，是帮你迅速判断：是某一方掌控了这根K线，还是多空双方陷入了僵持。图 1.1里有好几根K线可以说既算趋势K线、也算十字星。


> For trading purposes, it is useful to think of all bars are either trend bars or dojis (or nontrend bars, shown in Figure 1.1 with a "D"), and the labeling is loose. One bar with a small body could be a doji in one area of price action but a small trend bar in another. The only purpose for the distinction is to help you quickly assess whether one side is in control of the bar or if bulls and bears are at a stalemate. Several of the bars in Figure 1.1 could arguably be thought of as both trend bars and dojis.


图 1.2右侧的5分钟图上，从第1根K线开始连续出现了四根十字星，每一根的收盘价、高点和低点都依次走高。而15分钟图 1.2 左侧的那张图显示，它们在当时一个新的摆动低点处构成了一根多头反转K线，并伴随一次空头趋势通道线过靶（图中未画出）。单根十字星意味着多空双方都没有掌控市场，但趋势性十字星表明存在趋势。


> The 5-minute chart on the right of Figure 1.2 had four dojis in a row, starting at Bar 1, each With Trending closes, highs and lows. The 15-minute chart on the left of Figure 1.2 shows that they created a bull reversal bar at what was then a new swing low and a bear trend channel line overshoot (not drawn). Individual dojis mean that neither the bulls nor the bears are controlling the market, but trending dojis indicate a trend.


![图 1.2](figures/fig-01-02.png)


**图 1.2　趋势性十字星K线**


第4根K线是一根十字星，也就是一根K线构成的交易区间，但它仍然可以是一个好的建仓形态K线，具体取决于背景。在这里，它既是最终旗形失败（一个 ii 形态旗形，即连续两根内包K线），也是一个均线缺口K线的做空建仓形态，因此是一个可靠的信号。


> Bar 4 was a doji, which is a one-bar trading range, but it still can be a good setup bar, depending on context. Here, it was a Failed Final Flag (an ii flag) and an EMA Gap Bar short setup, and therefore a reliable signal.


正如十字星并不总是意味着市场没有趋势，一根趋势K线也并不总是意味着市场正在趋势中。图 1.3中的第1根K线是一根强多头趋势K线，它突破了一串十字星。然而，并没有后续行情。下一根K线向上越过那根趋势K线一个 tick，然后收在最低点。多头在这根空头停顿K线下方一个 tick 处离场，新的空头也在那里卖出，把它看成一次失败的多头突破。在没有更多偏多的价格行为出现之前，没人有兴趣买入，这导致市场下跌。多头试图用一根小多头趋势K线来守住多头突破K线的低点（第2根K线本是一个突破回调做多的建仓形态，但始终没有被触发），但市场还是跌穿了它的低点，这批刚进场的早期多头又一次在这里离场，更多新的空头进场了。到了这个时候，多头已经失败两次，如果没有明显有利于自己的价格行为，他们不会再愿意买入；他们和空头一样，都会去寻找至少两段下跌。交易者一整天都在找建仓形态。建仓形态是由一根或多根K线组成的图形形态，它让交易者相信：可以下一个委托，而且这笔委托有很好的机会带来一笔赚钱的交易。实际上，图上的每一根K线都是建仓形态，因为下一根K线总是可能成为任一方向上强行情的起点。如果这笔交易顺着近期或当前趋势的方向，它就是“顺势”；如果方向相反，它就是逆势建仓形态。举例来说，如果近期的趋势向上，你买入了，那么这个建仓形态就是顺势建仓形态；如果你反过来做空，那么你据以交易的建仓形态就是逆势建仓形态，你这笔空头就是一笔逆势交易。


> Just like dojis don't always mean the market is trendless, a trend bar does not always mean that the market is trending.
