> Bar 5 was a short setup for a failed High 1, and Bar 6 was a great bull trap. It was a failed High 2 and the long entry bar reversed into an outside bar down, trapping longs in and bears out. This outside bar acted like a bear trend bar and not just an outside bar. Because it is an outside bar, the entry bar and its failure happen within a minute or two of each other, not giving traders enough time to process the information. Within a bar or two, they realize that the market, in fact, has become a bear trend and the longs are hoping for a two-or three-bar pullback to exit with a smaller loss and the bears are hoping for the same rally to allow for a short entry with a smaller risk. What happens is that both sides start selling every two-or three-tick pullback, so a two-or three-bar rally does not come until the market has gone a long way.


![图 1.26](figures/fig-01-26.png)


**图 1.26　外包K线是两段式回调末端极好的顺势入场K线**


注意，这个高2做多是个糟糕的建仓形态，因为它前面六根K线里有五根是空头K线，另一根是十字星。单凭一个高2并不构成建仓形态，尤其在经历一次高潮顶部、可能还有一次主要趋势反转下跌之后。首先必须要有更早的强势，通常表现为一段突破趋势线的高1行情，或者至少是一根更早出现的强劲多头趋势K线。一根K线通常在收盘前几秒到一分钟甚至更久，就已经大致呈现出它最终的样子。如果你在K线收盘前入场，偶尔可能多赚一个 tick 左右。但是，每天总有一两次，你以为要出现的信号并没有出现，你会亏掉大约八个 tick。这意味着，大约需要八次按计划奏效的提前入场，才能抵消一次没成的，而这根本不会发生。在强趋势里，你可以提前顺势入场，而且多半不会有问题。不过，既然趋势很强，你对信号有十足的信心，那么等K线收盘、再在它之外挂止损单入场，并没有什么坏处。你不可能每根K线都去判断提前入场是否合适，因为你要做的重要决定实在太多。如果把这件事也加进你要考虑的清单，结果多半是每天错过很多好交易，错过的机会远远超过偶尔提前入场能多赚的那点。


> Note that the High 2 long was a terrible setup because five of the six prior bars were bear bars and the other bar was a doji. A High 2 alone is not a setup, especially after a climax top and possible major reversal down. There first has to be earlier strength, usually in the form of a High 1 leg that breaks a trendline or at least an earlier strong bull trend bar. A bar usually assumes something similar to its final appearance seconds to a minute or more before the bar closes. If you enter before the bar closes, you might occasionally make a tick or so more on your trade. However, once or twice every day, the signal that you thought was going to happen does not and you will lose about eight ticks. That means that you need about eight early entries to work as planned for every one that does not, and that simply won't happen. You can enter early With Trend in a strong trend, and you will likely be fine. However, when there is a strong trend, you have so much confidence in the signal that there is no downside to waiting for the bar to close and then entering on a stop beyond the bar. You cannot be deciding on every bar if an early entry is appropriate because you have too many other important decisions to make. If you add that to your list of things to think about, you will likely end up missing many good trades every day and forgo far more in missed opportunities than you could gain on an occasional early entry.


这一点在所有时间级别上都成立。例如，看一下日线图，你会看到很多K线开盘在低点附近、收盘却在中间。这些K线中的每一根，在当日某个时刻都曾是一根最新价位于高点的强劲多头趋势K线。如果你认定这根K线会收在高点、因此在接近高点时买入，结果它却收在中间，你就会意识到自己错了。你等于把一笔在收盘时永远不会入场的交易带回了家。


> This holds true for all time frames. For example, look at a daily chart, and you will see many bars that opened near the low but dosed in the middle. Each one of those bars was a strong bull trend bar with a last price on the high at some point during the day. If you bought under the assumption that the bar was going to dose on its high and bought near the high and instead it dosed in the middle, you would realize your mistake. You are carrying home a trade that you never would have entered at the end of the day.


5分钟图上经常出现两个常见问题。代价最大的是：在强趋势里试图抄底。通常情况下，趋势线突破之后你会看到一个更低的低点，交易者会期待一根强劲的反转K线，尤其当同时还出现空头趋势通道线过靶时。这根K线的形态摆得很漂亮，到第三分钟左右已经是一根强劲的多头反转K线。价格贴着这根K线的高点停了两三分钟，吸引越来越多想早点进场的逆势交易者——早进场，止损就能更小（他们的止损会放在这根K线下方）——可就在K线收盘前五秒，价格崩了，K线收在自己的低点上。所有那些想少冒一两个 tick 风险的提前做多者，最后亏掉两个点甚至更多。这些多头让自己被套进了一笔糟糕的交易。


> There are two common problems that regularly occur on the 5-minute chart. The most costly is when you try to pick a bottom in a strong trend. Typically you will see a Lower Low after a trendline break, and traders will be hoping for a strong reversal bar, especially if there is also a bear trend channel line overshoot. The bar sets up nicely and is a strong bull reversal bar by the third minute or so. The price is hanging near the high of the bar for a couple of minutes, attracting more and more Countertrend traders who want to get in early so that their stop will be smaller (their stop will be below the bar), but then with five seconds remaining before the bar doses, the price collapses, and the bar doses on its low. All of those early longs who were trying to risk a tick or two less end up losing two points or more. These longs let themselves get trapped into a bad trade.


另一个常见问题，是被关在一笔好交易之外。比如，你刚买入，这笔交易浮盈有三到五个 tick，但市场就是够不到六个，没法让你按四个 tick 的利润剥头皮出场，于是你开始紧张。你看着3分钟或5分钟图，距离它收盘还有大约10秒，图上是一根强劲的空头反转K线。于是你把保护性止损上移到那根K线下方一个 tick 处；就在K线收盘前，市场下跌打掉了你的止损，随后却在K线最后两秒里反弹了若干个 tick。接着，在下一根K线的头30秒内，市场迅速涨到6个 tick——聪明的交易者在那里部分止盈，而你只能站在场外看着。入场好，计划好，纪律差。你刚刚让自己被关在了一笔好交易之外。如果你按计划行事、在入场K线收盘前一直依靠最初那个止损，你本可以稳稳锁定利润。


> The other common problem is getting trapped out of a good trade. For example, if you just bought and your trade has had three to five ticks of open profit but the market just can't hit six, allowing you to scalp out with four ticks of profit, you start to become nervous. You look at the 3- or 5-minute chart with about 10 seconds before its bar doses, and it is a strong bear reversal bar. You then move your protective stop up to one tick below that bar, and just before the bar doses the market drops and hits your stop only to pop up several ticks in the final two seconds of the bar. Then, within the first 30 seconds of the next bar, the market quickly goes up to 6 ticks where smart traders took partial profits while you are sitting on the sidelines. Good entry, good plan, bad discipline. You just let yourself get trapped out of a good trade. If you had followed your plan and relied on your initial stop until the entry bar dosed, you would have secured your profit.


关于K线收盘，还有一点。要非常密切地关注每一根K线的收盘，尤其是入场K线以及之后的一两根。如果入场K线有六个 tick 高，你会很愿意看到它的实体在最后几秒里突然从一根两个 tick 的趋势K线变成一根四个 tick 的趋势K线。那样你多半会减少打算剥头皮出场的合约数量。接下来那一两根K线也是如此。如果收盘强劲，你就该比这些K线收盘疲软时更愿意多留一些合约做波段、持有到更多点数。


> There is one other point about bar doses. Pay very dose attention to the dose of every bar, especially for the entry bar and the bar or two later. If the entry bar is six ticks tall, you. would much prefer seeing the body suddenly increase from a two-tick trend bar to a four-tick trend bar in the final seconds of the bar. You will then likely reduce the number of contracts that you will scalp out. This is true for the next couple of bars as well. If there are strong closes, you should be more willing to swing more contracts and hold them for more points than if these bars had weak closes.


图 1.27中的5分钟 Emini 已经在强空头里走了好几周，现在它开始出现更大的回调，每一个新的更低的低点都有人在买，带来了有利可图的逆势交易。多头更有信心了，空头也越来越愿意止盈。左边的小图是3分钟图，右边那张是5分钟图的放大图。


> The 5-minute Emini in Figure 1.27 has been in a strong bear for weeks, and it is now starting to have bigger pullbacks and each new Lower Low is being bought, leading to profitable Countertrend trades. The bulls are more confident, and the bears are becoming more willing to take profits. The thumbnail on the left is a 3-minute chart, and the one on the right is a close-up of the 5-minute chart.


第5根K线突破了上方的一条趋势线，第8根K线则以不到一个 tick 的幅度越过了另一条。


> Bar 5 broke above a trendline, and Bar 8 exceeded another by a fraction of a tick.


第10根K线是一个 ii形态；如果只看实体，它其实是一个 iiii（连续四根内包K线，而且一根比一根小！），这可能引出一个极好的最终旗形失败，随后是一段两段式上涨，而且很可能在 EMA 上方出现一根缺口K线（它出现在第12根K线处），而这根K线多半会在回调到更高的低点之后被越过（也许就是第13根K线对趋势线的那次测试）。


> Bar 10 was an ii, and if you look at the bodies alone, it was an iiii (four inside bars in a row, each smaller than the prior!), which could lead to a great Failed Final Flag and then a two-legged rally and probably a gap bar above the EMA (it happened at Bar 12), which will likely be exceeded after a pullback to a Higher Low (maybe the Bar 13 test of the trendline).


第11根K线是一根强劲的多头反转K线，也是自一个更低的低点向上反转的第二次尝试（那个 iiii 是第一次）。这是一笔概率非常高的做多，但止损必须放在它的低点下方，比入场价低三个点。这比 Emini 里通常需要的止损更大（大多数交易通常两个点就够用），但价格行为显示这里就需要这么多。如果你心里发怵，就用一半的仓位规模做，但像这样强的建仓形态你必须接，并且打算留一半仓位做波段。


> Bar 1 1 was a strong bull reversal bar and a second attempt to reverse up from a Lower Low (the iiii was the first). This is a very high probability long, but the stop would have to be beneath its low, three points below the entry price. This is more than what is typically required in the Emini (normally two points works for most trades), but that is what the price action shows is needed. If you are nervous, just trade half-size, but you must take a strong setup like this one and plan on swinging half.


![图 1.27](figures/fig-01-27.png)


**图 1.27　强势空头，但已开始买入新低**


这是交易者为了降低风险去看更小时间级别图表时，所面对的常见问题的一个绝佳例子。第11根K线在3分钟图上同样有一根反转K线，但入场K线下方的止损被一根平顶平底的空头趋势K线打掉了——它的顶部和底部几乎都没有影线，说明卖方非常强。到了这一步，交易者很难把它和5分钟图上止损还没被打掉这件事协调起来。5分钟图上所需的止损太大，会让交易者更愿意提前离场、认下这笔亏损。如果这个交易者同时还在看3分钟图，他几乎肯定会亏损出场，而且会被那根强劲的空头趋势K线关在市场之外。3分钟图上的下一根K线是一根非常强劲的外包多头趋势K线，说明多头正在猛烈发力、造出一个更高的低点；但大多数被打掉止损的弱手多半会怕得不敢入场，而是去等回调。


> This is a perfect example of a common problem that traders face when they try to reduce risk by watching a smaller time frame chart. There was also a 3-minute reversal bar at Bar 11, but the stop below the entry bar was hit by a bear trend bar with shaved tops and bottoms, indicating very strong sellers. At this point, it would be very difficult to reconcile that with the 5-minute chart where the stop had not been hit. The large size of the stop required on the 5-minute chart would make traders more willing to exit early and take a loss. If a trader was also watching the 3-minute chart, he almost certainly would have exited with a loss, and he would have been trapped out of the market by that strong bear trend bar. The next bar on the 3-minute chart was a very strong outside bull trend bar, indicating that the bulls were violently asserting themselves in creating a Higher Low, but most of the weak hands who were stopped out would likely be so scared that they would not take the entry and instead wait for a pullback.


3分钟图上的止损猎杀在重要反转处非常常见，聪明的交易者把它们看成绝佳的机会，因为它们把弱势的多头关在市场之外，迫使他们追着市场往上买。只盯一张图来看、来做交易，始终是更好的做法，因为如果你同时看两张图、还要去调和它们之间的不一致，有时事情发生得太快，交易者来不及想清、也就来不及下单。有时候，只要对图表做点改动，价格行为就会变得更清楚。你可以换成K线图或折线图，或者基于成交量或 tick 数的图，或者换成更高、更低的时间级别，再或者干脆把图表打印出来。几只 ETF 也很有帮助。比如，SPY 的外观与 Emini 图几乎一模一样，而且有时候价格行为更清楚。


> Stop runs on the 3-minute chart are very common at important reversals, and smart traders look at them as great opportunities because they trap weak longs out of the market, forcing them to chase the market up. It is always better to just watch and trade off one chart because sometimes things happen too quickly for a trader to think fast enough to place his orders if he is watching two charts and trying to reconcile the inconsistencies. Sometimes the price action becomes clearer if you change something about the chart. You can switch to a bar or line chart or a chart based on volume or ticks, or a higher or lower time frame or simply print the chart. Several ETFs are also helpful. For example, the SPY is almost identical in appearance to the Emini chart and sometimes has clearer price action.


另外，从相反的角度看图表也可能有帮助。如果你看到的是一个牛旗，但总觉得哪里不太对，不妨看看 SDS——它是按 SPY 的反向走势构建的 ETF（不过带两倍杠杆）。如果你去看它，可能会发现自己在 Emini 和 SPY 上看到的那个牛旗，在 SDS 上现在看起来像是一个圆弧底。如果真是这样，明智的做法就是别买 Emini 上那个旗形，而是等更多的价格行为展开（比如等突破，然后在突破失败时做空）。有时候，形态在其他股指期货上更清楚，比如 Emini 纳斯达克100，或者它的 ETF——QQQQ（纳斯达克100的 ETF），或者它的双倍反向产品 QID；但通常不值得去看这些，更好的做法是坚持看 Emini，有时再加上 SDS。


> Also, it can be helpful to consider the chart from an opposite perspective. If you are seeing a bull flag but something doesn't seem quite right, consider looking at the SDS, which is an ETF that is based on the inverse of the SPY (but with twice the leverage). If you look at it, you might discover that the bull flag that you were seeing on the Emini and SPY might now look like a rounding bottom on the SDS. If it does, you would be wise not to buy the Emini flag and instead wait for more price action to unfold (like waiting for the breakout and then shorting if it fails). Sometimes patterns are clearer on other stock index futures, like the Emini Nasdaq-100, or its ETF, the QQQQ, or its double inverse, the QID, but it is usually not worth looking at these and it is better to stick with the Emini and sometimes the SDS.


![图 1.28](figures/fig-01-28.png)


**图 1.28　SDS 本质上就是 Emini 的反向走势图，能帮你判断 Emini 的建仓形态**


图 1.28中最上面那张 Emini 图与中间那张 SPY 图基本上完全一样，但 SPY 上的价格行为有时更容易读。最下面那张是 SDS，它是一只与 SPY 反向的 ETF（带两倍杠杆）。有时 SDS 图会让你重新考虑自己对 Emini 图的解读。日线图上的底部通常需要从低点起的第二次反转，才能说服足够多的交易者把这个市场当成可能的新多头行情来交易。这第二次入场几乎总是比第一次入场更有可能做成一笔盈利的交易。卖方正在第二次尝试把价格压下去；如果市场在两次尝试中都失败了，它通常就会试着朝相反方向去做。


> The top chart of the Emini in Figure 1.28 is essentially identical to that of the SPY in the middle chart, but the price action on the SPY is sometimes easier to read. The bottom chart is the SDS, which is an ETF that is the inverse of the SPY (with twice the leverage). Sometimes the SDS chart will make you reconsider your read of the Emini chart. Bottoms on the daily chart usually require a second reversal off the low to convince enough traders to trade the market as a possible new bull. This second entry is almost always more likely to result in a profitable trade than is a first entry. The sellers are making a second attempt to drive the price down and if the market fails in two attempts to do something, it usually will attempt to do the opposite.


如果任何时间级别上的二次入场给你的价格比第一次更好，就要怀疑它可能是个陷阱。大多数好的二次入场，价格都与第一次相同或更差。二次入场交易者是那种进场较晚、想尽量减小风险的人，而市场通常会让你为多出来的那份信息多付一点。如果它反而少收你的钱，那它可能是在设局，准备用一次失败的高2/低2把你的钱拿走。


> If the second entry on any time frame is letting you in at a better price than the first, be suspicious that it might be a trap. Most good second entries are at the same price or worse. A second entry trader is someone entering late, trying to minimize risk, and the market usually makes you pay a little more for that additional information. If it is charging you less, it ght be setting you up to steal your money in a failed High/Low 2.


寻找二次入场的交易者更激进、也更有信心，往往会到更小时间级别的图上去入场。这通常导致5分钟图上的交易者在许多其他人已经入场之后才进场，入场价因此更差一点。如果市场给你的价格更好，你就该怀疑自己漏掉了什么，并考虑不做这笔交易。大多数时候，好的成交价等于一笔糟糕的交易（而糟糕的成交价等于一笔好的交易！）。


> Traders looking for second entries are more aggressive and confident, and will often enter on smaller time frame charts. This usually results in traders on the 5-minute charts entering after many other traders have already entered, making the entry a little worse. If the market is letting you in at a better price, you should suspect that you are missing something and consider not taking the trade. Most of the time, a good fill equals a bad trade (and a bad fill equals a good trade!).


如果你正在对一段行情做反向操作——比如在多头行情里买回调——而这段行情大约有四根强劲的趋势K线，或者两三根大实体趋势K线，那么动能就太强，你不该逆着它下单。更好的做法是等来一个入场信号、然后不做它，接着再等第二根回调K线，在市场第二次尝试反转时入场。


> If you are fading a move, buying a pullback in a bull, for example, and the move had about four strong trend bars or two or three large trend bars, there is too much momentum for you to be placing an order in the opposite direction. It is better to wait for an entry, then don't take it, and then wait for a second pullback bar and then enter on the market's second attempt to reverse.


既然好建仓形态里的二次入场通常会成功，那么一旦有一次失败，就要假定自己读错了市场，不要去做第三次入场——除非那是楔形（一次失败的趋势通道线突破）。


> Since second entries in good setups usually succeed, if one fails, assume that you are reading the market incorrectly and do not take a third entry unless it is a Wedge (a failed trend channel line breakout).


图 1.29这一天有很多笔二次入场交易，除了一笔以外，价格都与第一次入场相同或更差。看看第10根K线的做多。市场让你买入的价格比那些在第9根K线买入的交易者还好一个 tick。一般而言，“成交好，交易糟”这句格言在这里是适用的。只要市场给你便宜货，就要假定自己把图读错了；通常更好的做法是不做这笔交易。


> There were many second entry trades today in Figure 1.29, and all but one were at the same price or a worse price than the first entry. Look at the Bar 10 long. The market is letting you buy at one tick better than the traders who bought at Bar 9. In general, the "Good fill, bad trade" maxim applies. Whenever the market is offering you a bargain, assume that you are reading the chart incorrectly, and usually it is better not to take the trade.


![图 1.29](figures/fig-01-29.png)


**图 1.29　二次入场通常是极好的信号**


图 1.30中的第1根K线是在当日新高处的低1做空，但它前面跟着五根多头趋势K线，向上的动能太强，不该考虑卖出。聪明的交易者会先等等，看多头在第二次上涨尝试中会不会失败，然后再做空——这就发生在第2根K线的第二次做空入场处。


> Bar 1 in Figure 1.30 was a Low 1 short at a new high on the day, but it followed five bull trend bars, which is too much upward momentum to be looking to sell. Smart traders would wait to see if the bulls would fail in a second attempt to rally before going short, and this happened on the second short entry at Bar 2.


第3根K线是在当日新低处的第一次做多入场，但已经有六根K线没有出现多头收盘，更合理的做法是等第二次做多入场，它就出现在第4根K线。一般而言，与你想做的方向相反的趋势K线达到四根或更多，就意味着通常更该选二次入场。


> Bar 3 was a first entry long on a new low of the day, but after six bars without a bullish close, it makes more sense to wait for a second long entry, which occurred on Bar 4. In general, four or more trend bars against your intended direction means that a second entry is usually preferable.


第5根K线是一个高2，但它前面跟着四根空头趋势K线，向下的动能太强。二次入场始终没有出现，所以聪明的交易者靠等待避免了一次亏损——尽管在一段长行情之后，从 ii 旗形（7根K线之前）里反转出来做多，通常是一笔不错的交易。


> Bar 5 was a High 2, but it followed four bear trend bars, which is too much down momentum. A second entry never developed, so smart traders averted a loss by waiting, although going long on a reversal out of an ii flag (7 bars earlier) after a long move is usually a good trade.


第7根K线的 ii 形态可能是一次最终旗形失败。交易者本来可以在第8根K线做多，但它前面那根反转K线与更前一根重叠太多，而且自第6根K线起的下跌太强。第9根K线给出了二次入场，它紧随前一根K线试图下跌的尝试之后。


> The Bar 7 ii was a possible Failed Final Flag. Traders could have gone long on Bar 8, but the prior reversal bar had too much overlap with the bar before it and the move down from Bar 6 was too strong. Bar 9 offered a second entry, following the prior bar's attempt to sell off.


第10根K线是低1，它是自第8根K线低点以来、在两根空头K线之后出现的，但此前已有六根低点更高的K线，说明多头力量太强。二次入场出现在第11根空头反转K线处。


> Bar 10 was a Low 1 following two earlier bear bars since the Bar 8 low, but there were six bars with higher lows, indication too much bullish strength. There was a second entry at the Bar 11 bear reversal bar .


![图 1.30](figures/fig-01-30.png)


**图 1.30　市场强势时，先等二次入场再做反向操作**


如果你看任何一张图时想到：当初要是接了那个最初入场，自己现在还会拿着这笔交易的波段部分，那你就该以市价入场。不过，你只该按当初接了最初入场、如今仍会持有的那个股数或合约数入场，并且使用同样的移动止损。举个例子，如果你看到 GS 正在走一段强趋势，当初以300股接了最初入场，而现在你只会还剩下100股、保护性止损在 $1.50之外，那你就该以市价买入100股，并挂上 $1.50的保护性止损。从逻辑上说，现在买入一个波段规模的仓位，与从更早的入场持有波段仓位，没有任何区别。虽然在情绪上，把有浮盈的这笔交易想成是在拿别人的钱冒险，可能更容易接受，但那不是事实。钱是你的，你现在承担的风险，与现在买入、承担同样的 $1.50风险并无不同。交易者明白这一点，下单时不会犹豫。如果他做不到，那他就是并不相信自己当初入场至今还会留着任何股票，或者他需要处理一下这个情绪问题。


> If you look at any chart and think that, if you had taken the original entry, you would still be holding the swing portion of your trade, then you need to enter at the market. However, you should only enter with the number of shares or contracts that you would still be holding had you taken the original entry, and you should use the same trailing stop. For example, if you see a strong trend underway in GS, and had you taken the original entry with 300 shares and you now would only be holding 100 shares with your protective stop at $1.50 away, you should buy 100 shares at the market and place a $1.50 protective stop. Logically, buying a swing size portion now or holding a swing position from an earlier entry doesn't make a difference. Although it might be easier emotionally to think of the trade with the open profit as risking someone else's money, that is not the reality. It is your money, and what you are risking is no different from buying now and risking the same $1.50. A trader knows this and will place the trade without hesitation. If he does not, then he simply does not believe that he would still be holding any shares had he entered earlier, or he needs to work on this emotional issue.


在图 1.31中，GS 昨天以一段强势空头收尾，而它可能在收盘前就已经见底——当时临近收盘的那波上涨突破了空头趋势线。第1根K线处出现了一次二次做多入场，它发生在一根强劲的多头趋势K线和一个高2之后。


> In Figure 1.31 GS ended in a strong bear yesterday that might have bottomed before the close when the rally into the close broke the bear trendline. There was a second long entry at Bar 1 following a strong bull trend bar and a High 2.


![图 1.31](figures/fig-01-31.png)


**图 1.31　进入强趋势永远不嫌晚**


今天开盘后抛售了三根K线，测试 EMA 和昨天的收盘价，随后反转向上了，形成一次开盘反转，也是一次两段式横盘修正之后的更高的低点。


> Today's open sold off for three bars to test the EMA and yesterday's close and then reversed up for an Opening Reversal and a Higher Low after a two-legged sideways correction.


如果交易者错过了那笔做多，在第4根K线附近、在一连串多头K线之后看到这张图，他多半会希望自己当时抓住了开盘，那样至少手里还有仓位的波段部分在做着。如果他平时做300股，而在第4根K线附近，按他错过的那笔第3根K线入场、带着保本止损算，本来只会剩下100股，那他就该以市价买入100股，并把止损放在第3根信号K线的高点处（也许放在高点下方10美分，因为 GS 经常扫止损）。他还应该留意停顿和回调，好加仓。在第6根K线之后的高2处加仓之后，他可以把整个仓位的止损移到第6根信号K线下方一个 tick 处，然后一路向上移动。


> If a trader had missed the long and saw this chart around Bar 4 after a series of bull bars, he would probably be wishing that he had caught the open so that he would at least have the swing portion of his position still working. If he normally trades 300 shares and he would normally only have 100 left around Bar 4 with a breakeven stop from the Bar 3 entry that he missed, he should buy 100 shares at the market and use that stop at the high of the Bar 3 signal bar (maybe 10 cents below the high, since GS often runs stops). He should also look for pauses and pullbacks to add on. After adding on at the High 2 after Bar 6, he could move the stop for the entire position to one tick below the Bar 6 signal bar and then trail it up.


迟到入场并使用原来的止损，与持有最初仓位里做波段的那一部分、用同一个保护性止损，完全是一回事。


> Entering late and using the original stop is absolutely identical to being long the swing portion of the original position, using the same protective stop.


# 第 2 章　趋势线与趋势通道

*Chapter 2. Trendlines and Trend Channels*


趋势线和趋势通道线都是直线，它们与趋势平行，但位于趋势的两侧，构成一个把价格行为包在里面的通道。趋势线最常用来建立顺势交易的建仓形态，而趋势通道线最有用的地方是找出可交易的反转。曲线太主观，所以在你想快速下单时，需要花太多心思去琢磨。在沿着趋势方向于回调中找入场点、或者在趋势线被突破后朝反方向找入场点时，趋势线是最有用的。趋势线可以用摆动点来画，也可以用最佳拟合办法来画，比如线性回归计算，或者干脆迅速画一条最接近的近似线。趋势线也可以先画成某条趋势通道线的平行线，再拖到K线的趋势线那一侧，但这种做法很少需要——因为这样生成的任何信号，通常本来也建立在更常见的价格行为分析类型之上。有时候，最佳拟合趋势线只用蜡烛线实体来画、忽略影线；这在楔形形态里很常见，而楔形形态往往并不具备楔形的形状。多数时候并不需要真的去画一条线，因为这些线通常显而易见。如果你确实画了线，通常在确认市场已经测试过它之后，过一会儿就可以把它擦掉。


> Both trendlines and trend channel lines are straight lines that are parallel to the trend but on opposite sides of the trend, forming a channel that contains the price action. Trendlines most often set up With Trend trades, and trend channel lines are most helpful finding tradable reversals. Curved lines are too subjective and therefore require too much thought when you are trying to place trades quickly. A trendline is most helpful when looking for entries in the direction of the trend on pullbacks and in the opposite direction after the trendline is broken. Trendlines can be drawn using swing points or best fit techniques such as linear regression calculations or simply quickly drawing a best approximation. They also can be drawn as a parallel of a trend channel line and then dragged to the trendline side of the bars, but this approach is rarely needed since any signals generated are usually also based on more common types of price action analysis. Sometimes the best fit trendline is drawn just using the candle bodies and ignoring the tails; this is common in Wedge patterns, which often do not have a Wedge shape. Most of the time it is not necessary to actually draw a line since the lines are usually obvious. If you do draw a line, you usually can erase it moments after you verify that the market has tested it.


一旦趋势由一系列依次走高或走低的高点和低点确立起来，最赚钱的交易就是顺着趋势线的方向做，直到趋势线被突破。每当市场回调到趋势线附近的区域——哪怕它未及靶位或过靶了这条趋势线——都要寻找从趋势线上反转的迹象，然后顺着趋势方向入场。即使趋势线已经被突破，只要它此前生效了几个小时或更久，那么在回调之后，趋势极值点被测试的可能性就很大。这次测试之后，可能是趋势延续，可能是趋势反转，也可能是市场进入交易区间。关于趋势线突破，最重要的一点是：它是市场不再只由单方（买方或卖方）控制的第一信号，此后双向交易的可能性大大增加。每一次趋势线突破之后，都会出现一个新的摆动点，用来画新的趋势线。通常，每一条后续的趋势线坡度都更小，说明趋势正在失去动能。到了某个时刻，随着市场控制权从空头转到多头（或者反过来），反方向的趋势线会变得更重要。


> Once a trend has been established by a series of trending highs and lows, the most profitable trades are in the direction of the trendline until the trendline is broken. Every time the market pulls back to the area around the trendline, even if it undershoots or overshoots the trendline, look for a reversal off of the trendline and then enter in the direction of the trend. Even after a trendline breaks, if it has been in effect for a couple of hours or more, the chances are high that the trend extreme will get tested after a pullback. The test can be followed by the trend continuing, the trend reversing, or the market entering a trading range. The single most important point about a trendline break is that it is the first sign that the market is no longer being controlled by just one side (buyers or sellers) and the chances of further two sided trading is now much greater. After every trendline break, there will be a new swing point upon which to base a new line. Typically, each successive line has a smaller slope, indicating that the trend is losing momentum. At some point, trendlines in the opposite direction will become more important as control of the market switches from the bears to the bulls or vice versa.


趋势线突破的力度，能反映逆势交易者的力度。逆势行情越大、越快，市场在回头测试趋势极值点之后发生反转的可能性就越高（例如，在测试多头高点时形成更低的高点或更高的高点之后）。


> The strength of the trendline break provides an indication of the strength of the Countertrend traders. The bigger and faster the Countertrend move, the more likely that a reversal will occur after the market comes back to test the trend's extreme (for example, after a Lower High or a Higher High in the test of the high of the bull).


把跳空开盘和任何一根大趋势K线都看成实际上是突破，会很有帮助，而且每一个都应该当作单根K线趋势来对待，因为突破常常失败，一旦出现建仓形态，你就得准备好反向操作它们。此后几根K线里只要出现任何横盘，就会破坏这个趋势。通常，这些K线会形成一个旗形，随后是一段走出旗形的顺势行情；但有时候突破会失败，市场会反转。既然这些横盘K线“突破”了趋势线，只要有好的信号K线，你就可以考虑反向操作这个趋势。


> It is helpful to consider a gap opening and any large trend bar to effectively be breakouts and each one should be treated as if it is a one-bar trend, since breakouts commonly fail and you need to be prepared to fade them if there is a setup. Any sideways movement over the next few bars will break the trend. Usually, those bars will be setting up a flag and then be followed by a With Trend move out ofthe flag, but sometimes the breakout will fail and the market will reverse. Since the sideways bars "broke" the trendline, you can look to fade the trend if there is a good signal bar.


图 2.1中哪些趋势线是有效的？你能看到的每一条都有产生一笔交易的潜力。找出你能找到的每一个摆动点，看看有没有更早的一个点能与它用趋势线连起来，然后把这条线向右延伸，看价格在穿透或触及这条线时如何反应。注意每一条后续的趋势线都倾向于变得更平，直到某个时刻，反方向的趋势线变得更重要。


> Which trendlines are valid in Figure 2.1? Every one of them that you can see has the potential to generate a trade. Look for every swing point that you can find and see if there is an earlier one that can be connected with a trendline, and then extend the line to the right and see how price responds when it penetrates or touches the line. Notice how each successive trendline tends to become flatter until some point when trendlines in the opposite direction become more important.


在实际操作中，当你看到一条可能的趋势线、又不确定它离当前K线有多远时，就把它画出来，看市场有没有打到它，然后很快擦掉。交易时，你不希望图上的线停留超过几秒钟，因为你不想要干扰。你需要专注于K线，看它们走到线附近时如何表现，而不是盯着这条线。


> In actual practice, when you see a possible trendline and you are not certain how far it is from the current bar, draw it to see if the market has hit it and then quickly erase the line. You don't want lines on your chart for more than a few seconds when trading because you don't want distractions. You need to focus on the bars and see how they behave once near the line, and not focus on the line.


随着趋势推进，逆势运动会突破趋势线，而这些突破通常都会失败，从而形成顺势入场的建仓形态。每一次突破的失败，都会成为新的一条更长、坡度更平缓的趋势线的第二个点。最终，失败的突破本身也失败，形成突破回调，而这些回调让人可以画出反方向的趋势线。主要趋势线被突破之后，反方向的趋势线变得更重要，而到那时，趋势很可能已经反转了。


> As a trend progresses, Countertrend moves break the trendlines, and usually the breakouts fail, setting up With Trend entries. Each breakout failure becomes the second point for the creation of a new, longer trendline with a shallower slope. Eventually failed breakouts fail, creating Breakout Pullbacks, and these allow for the drawing of trendlines in the opposite direction. After the major trendline is broken, the trendlines in the opposite direction become more important, and at that point the trend has likely reversed.


![图 2.1](figures/fig-02-01.png)


**图 2.1　所有趋势线都很重要**


趋势线可以借助趋势通道线来画，但这样很少能提供别的、用更常见的价格行为分析看不出来的交易。


> A trendline can be drawn from a trend channel line, but this rarely provides trades that are not already apparent using other more common price action analysis.


在图 2.2中，用第1根到第4根K线的空头趋势通道线来作平行线，这条平行线被拖到价格对侧，并锚定在第2根K线的高点上（因为这样它就能包含第1根与第4根K线之间——也就是趋势通道线起点与终点之间——的全部价格）。


> Here in Figure 2.2, a bear trend channel line from Bars 1 to 4 is used to create a parallel, and the parallel is dragged to the opposite side of the price and anchored at the Bar 2 high (because this then contains all of the prices between the Bars 1 and 4 beginning and end of the trend channel line).


第6根K线是反转那条线之上突破的第二次尝试，因此是一个很好的做空建仓形态。


> Bar 6 is a second attempt to reverse the break above that line and therefore a good short setup.


这条趋势线与用第2根和第5根K线的高点画出的趋势线几乎无法区分，所以对寻找做空机会的交易者来说毫无帮助。列出它只是为了完整。


> The trendline is almost indistinguishable from the trendline created from the highs of Bars 2 and 5 and so adds nothing to a trader looking for a short. It is shown only for completeness.


第6根K线同时也是对第3根和第5根K线趋势通道线的一次失败过靶，这让第6根K线处的做空成为决斗线交易的例子（趋势线与趋势通道线相交，且方向相反）。


> Bar 6 was also a failed overshoot of the Bars 3 and 5 trend channel line, making the Bar 6 short an example of a Dueling Lines trade (trendline and trend channel lines intersecting and in opposite directions).


图 2.3中第2根和第3根K线的趋势通道线可以平移并锚定到第1根K线，画出一条趋势线，用来大致判断可交易的反弹可能出现在哪里。一次两段式回调过靶了这条趋势线，并在1分钟 Emini 小型合约上反转向上。


> The trend channel line from Bars 2 and 3 in Figure 2.3 can be moved and anchored to Bar 1 to create a trendline that can give an idea of where a tradable bounce might occur. A two-legged pullback overshot the trendline and reversed up on the 1-minute Emini.


![图 2.2](figures/fig-02-02.png)


**图 2.2　借助趋势通道线画出的趋势线**


![图 2.3](figures/fig-02-03.png)


**图 2.3　作为趋势通道线平行线而画出的趋势线**


第2根K线是一根大K线，应该看成单根K线趋势。任何横盘运动会突破这条趋势线，但通常都会形成旗形，就像这里一样。不过，反转很常见，只要有好的信号K线就可以交易。


> Bar 2 is a big bar and should be considered to be a one-bar trend. Any sideways movement will break the trendline but usually will set up a flag, as it did here. However, reversals are common and can be traded if there is a good signal bar.


![图 2.4](figures/fig-02-04.png)


**图 2.4　趋势通道线有时能大致给出右肩的高度**


当可能形成头肩形态时，横跨颈线（图 2.4中的第2根和第6根K线）画一条趋势通道线并拖到左肩（第1根K线），有时能大致给出右肩应该形成的位置（第8根K线）。这不太重要，因为在决定从哪里入场时，最近的几根K线总是重要得多。列出这张图只是为了完整。与任何头肩形态无关，交易者也会做空第8根K线那个更低的高点，因为它与第5根K线构成双顶熊旗，是一个小楔形，还是从第6根K线低点开始的急速行情（spike）与通道上涨行情的顶部。微型趋势线是任何时间级别上的一条趋势线，横跨2根到约10根K线，其中大多数K线都触及或接近这条趋势线，随后其中一根K线出现一次穿过趋势线的假突破。这次假突破形成顺势入场，是多头中一个高1做多、或空头中一个低1做空里最可靠的类型。这些是很小（通常只有一到两根K线长）但很强的牛旗和熊旗。如果它在一两根K线内失败，那么通常会出现一笔逆势交易，实际上就变成突破回调入场和最终旗形失败。绝大多数微型趋势线假突破都是1分钟图上的高1/低1与高2/低2回调，但如果你跟1分钟图，很可能亏钱，因为你无法把每一笔交易都做上，而且总会挑中太多烂樱桃〔译注：cherry picking 指在众多机会里挑挑拣拣，结果挑中的偏偏是最差的那几个〕。当趋势很强、没有K线回调、你又急着进场时，你可以在1分钟图上找一个高2/低2回调，但在5分钟或3分钟图上于微型趋势线突破失败处入场也一样容易。任何穿过它的动作很可能也是1分钟级别的回调，所以在突破失败处入场（在多头中，就在那根跌破趋势线的K线的高点上方一个最小报价单位处入场）。小的陡趋势线，哪怕只用两根连续K线画出，也常常提供顺势交易的建仓形态。如果趋势很陡，有时候一根小回调K线或一根停顿K线就能穿透一条很小的趋势线，而一旦穿透，它就能成为顺势入场的信号K线。有些穿透在 Emini 上还不到一个最小报价单位，但依然有效。


> When a possible Head and Shoulders pattern is setting up, a trend channel line drawn across the neckline (Bars 2 and 6 in Figure 2.4) and dragged to the left shoulder (Bar 1) sometimes gives an approximation of where the right shoulder should form (Bar 8). This is of minor importance since the most recent bars are always much more important in deciding where to enter. This chart is included only for completeness. Independent of any Head and Shoulders pattern, a trader would short the Bar 8 Lower High because it was a Double Top Bear Flag with Bar 5, a small Wedge, and the top of a Spike and Channel rally from the Bar 6 low. A Micro Trendline is a trendline on any time frame that is drawn across from 2 to about 10 bars where most of the bars touch or are close to the trendline, and then one of the bars has a false breakout through the trendline. This false breakout sets up a With Trend entry and is the most reliable type of a High 1 long in a bull or a Low 1 short in a bear. These are tiny (usually just one or two bars long) but strong bull and bear flags. If it fails within a bar or two, then there is usually a Countertrend trade, which effectively becomes a Breakout Pullback entry and a Failed Final Flag. The vast majority of Micro Trendline false breakouts are 1 minute High/Low I and 2 pullbacks, but if you follow the 1 minute chart you will likely lose money because you will not be able to take all the trades and you will invariably pick too many bad cherries. When a trend is strong with no bar pullbacks and you are eager to get in, you can look at a 1-minute chart for a High/Low 2 pullback, but it is just as easy to enter on a 5- or 3-minute Micro Trendline failed breakout. Any poke through it is also likely a 1-minute pullback, so enter on the failed breakout (in a bull, enter at one tick above the bar that dips below the trendline). Small, steep trendlines, even drawn using two consecutive bars, often provide setups for With Trend trades. If the trend is steep, sometimes a small Pullback Bar or a pause bar can penetrate a tiny trendline and when it does, it can become a signal bar for a With Trend entry. Some of the penetrations are smaller than one tick in the Eminis, but are still valid.


如果突破回调入场失败——比如在下跌行情中遇到空头微型趋势线——那就看这些K线实体的大小。如果这些K线是趋势K线，那么这一次二次失败（先突破失败、接着突破回调失败）意味着市场很可能是在给你一个可交易的低2做空。如果这些K线更像十字星，那么市场很可能会进入铁丝网，但概率仍然偏向向下突破。如果你不确定，那就等，因为很可能大多数交易者也不确定，铁丝网是大概率结果。


> If the Breakout Pullback entry fails, for example in a falling market with a bear Micro Trendline, then look at the size of the bodies of the bars. If the bars are trend bars, then this second failure (the failed breakout and then the failed breakout Pullback), the odds are high that the market is giving you a tradable Low 2 short. If the bars have more of a doji look, then the market will likely enter Barb Wire, but the odds still favor a downside breakout. If you are not certain, then wait because it is likely that most traders will not be certain and Barb Wire is likely.


微型趋势线可以用来构造微型趋势通道线，这些通道线同样能形成突破失败后的反转。微型趋势通道线通常画成微型趋势线的平行线。不过，有时候在微型趋势线形成的过程中，K线的另一端也全都靠近一条微型趋势线，这条线可以在这一段行情的前两三根K线形成之后画出来。


> Micro Trendlines can be used to create Micro Trend Channel Lines, which also can set up a reversal of a failed breakout. The Micro Trend Channel Line is usually created as a parallel of a Micro Trendline. However, sometimes as the Micro Trendline is forming, the opposite ends of the bars are also all close to a Micro Trendline that can be drawn after the first two or three bars of the leg form.


最后，当一条微型趋势线包含一个非常狭窄的通道并持续较长时间，比如约十根K线时，突破失败本身再失败、变成一次突破回调反转的概率会大幅上升，这种反转至少应该够做一次剥头皮。当它出现在一段较长的趋势行情之后时，尤其如此。


> Finally, when a Micro Trendline contains a very tight channel for an extended period, like about ten bars, the odds increase substantially that the breakout failure will fail and become a Breakout Pullback reversal that should be good for at least a scalp. This is especially true when it develops after an extended trend move.


微型趋势线能在一天里产生许多剥头皮机会，尤其是在1分钟图上，而1分钟图很少值得交易。图 2.5左边的图是一张1分钟 Emini 小型合约图，数字对应右边5分钟图上的同一批K线。两者都显示，微型趋势线的突破失败可以带来有利可图的反向操作。1分钟图上还有其他交易没有画出来，因为这张图的目的只是想说明5分钟微型趋势线如何对应1分钟图上更明显、更长的趋势线；所以，如果你能读5分钟图，就不必再额外去看1分钟图来下单。其中许多交易本来都能在1分钟图上成为盈利的剥头皮。


> Micro trendlines can generate many scalps during the day, especially on the 1-minute chart, which is seldom worth trading. The chart on the left in Figure 2.5 is a 1-minute Emini chart, and the numbers correspond to the same bars on the 5-minute chart on the right. Both show that failed breakouts from tiny trendlines can result in profitable fades. There are other trades on the 1-minute chart that are not shown because the purpose of this figure is only to show how 5-minute Micro Trendlines correspond to more obvious, longer trendlines on the 1-minute chart, so if you can read the 5-minute chart, you do not have to additionally look at the 1-minute chart to place your orders. Many of these trades could have been profitable scalps on the 1-minute chart.


![图 2.5](figures/fig-02-05.png)


**图 2.5　微型趋势线能创造绝佳的入场点**


注意，5分钟图上好几处微型趋势线突破都容易被忽略，幅度还不到一个最小报价单位。例如，第3、5、6、7根K线都是5分钟图上失败的微型趋势线突破，对大多数交易者来说根本看不见，但第5根K线那一处特别重要，它带来了一次很好的做空剥头皮。那是第二次试图向上突破一条空头趋势线的失败（第3根K线是第一次）。


> Note that several breaks of Micro Trendlines on the 5-minute chart are easy to overlook and are less than one tick in size. For example, Bars 3, 5, 6, and 7 are failed Micro Trendline breaks on the 5-minute chart that would be invisible to most traders, but the one at Bar 5 is particularly significant and led to a good short scalp. It was the second failed attempt to break above a bear trendline (Bar 3 was the first).


价格行为交易哪怕在最小级别上也都有效。注意1分钟图上第8根K线是一个更高的高点突破回测做多建仓形态，而且尽管入场之后两根K线市场就回落测试第8根信号K线的低点，信号K线下方的保护性止损也不会被触发。还要注意，在1分钟图的这一段里还有一个更小的“主要反转”。这里有一段很小的多头趋势，由图表低点起的一条多头微型趋势线标示，然后在第7根K线处趋势线被突破，接着是对这个小多头趋势极值点的更高的高点测试。由于形态这么小，跌到第8根K线的“趋势反转”只是一次剥头皮，这本就是意料之中的。


> Price action trading works even at the tiniest level. Note how Bar 8 on the 1-minute chart was a Higher High Breakout Test long setup and that although the market came down to test the Bar 8 signal bar low two bars after entry, the protective stop below the signal bar would not have been hit. Also note that there was also an even smaller "major reversal" in this segment of the 1-minute chart. There was a tiny bull trend, indicated by the bull Micro Trendline up from the low of the chart, then a break of the trendline at Bar 7, and then a Higher High test of the tiny bull trend extreme. Since the pattern is so small, the "trend reversal" down to Bar 8 was just a scalp, as should be expected.


即使在陡趋势中只用两三根连续K线画出的趋势线，在出现一次立即反转的小突破时，也能形成顺势入场的建仓形态。每一次新的突破都会成为一条更长、更平缓的趋势线上的第二个点，直到最终反方向的趋势线变得更重要，而到那时趋势已经反转了。


> Even trendlines created using just two or three consecutive bars in a steep trend can setup With Trend entries when there is a small break that immediately reverses. Each new break becomes the second point in a longer, flatter trendline until eventually trendlines in the opposite direction become more important, and at that point the trend has reversed.


图 2.6中的第1根K线跌破了一条三根K线趋势线并反转向上，在前一根K线上方一个最小报价单位处形成做多入场。


> Bar 1 in Figure 2.6 dipped below a three-bar trendline and reversed up, creating a long entry at one tick above the prior bar.


第2根K线跌破了一条六根K线趋势线。交易者会在其高点上方挂一张买入止损单。没成交时，他们会把止损单移到下一根K线的高点，并在第3根K线成交。顺带一提，紧挨着第2根K线之前的那根K线是一个可能的做空建仓形态，依据是一条微型趋势通道线（未画出），它是通向第1根K线的那条三根K线微型趋势线的平行线。上升动能太强，不做第二次入场就做空不行，但这说明微型趋势通道线如何能形成逆势交易的建仓形态。第4根K线是一根小的内包K线，向下延伸并突破了二根K线趋势线（穿透没有画出）。买入是在这根小内包K线高点上方一个最小报价单位处的止损单。


> Bar 2 dipped below a six-bar trendline. Traders would place a buy stop above its high. When not filled, they would move the stop to the high of the next bar and would be filled on Bar 3. Incidentally, the bar before Bar 2 was a possible short setup based on a Micro Trend Channel Line (not shown) that is a.parallel of the three-bar Micro Trendline leading up to Bar 1. The upward momentum was too strong for a short without a second entry but this illustrates how Micro Trend Channel Lines can set up countertrend trades. Bar 4 was a small inside bar that extended below a two-bar trendline (the penetration is not shown). The buy is on a stop at one tick above the high of the small inside bar.


第5根K线突破了当天的主要趋势线（任何持续约一个小时左右的趋势线都更重要），所以交易者会认为两段式回调的可能性更大。在第5根K线之后那根K线向上突破空头趋势线之后，做空会在第6根K线那个更低的高点处被触发。当K线是像第5根K线之后那样的小十字星K线时，通常最好等更大的趋势K线出现再做更多交易，但这些趋势线反转在 Amazon 上仍然带来了30到50美分的盈利剥头皮。


> Bar 5 broke the major trendline of the day (any trendline lasting about an hour or so is more significant), so traders would be thinking that a two-legged pullback was more likely. After the break above the bear trendline on the bar following Bar 5, a short would be triggered on the Bar 6 Lower High. When bars are small doji bars like those following Bar 5, it is usually best to wait for bigger trend bars before taking more trades, but these trendline reversals still led to profitable scalps of 30 to 50 cents in Amazon.


![图 2.6](figures/fig-02-06.png)


**图 2.6　微型趋势线可以只有两三根K线长**


![图 2.7](figures/fig-02-07.png)


**图 2.7　强趋势中的微型趋势线**


强趋势中的小趋势线，即使是用相邻K线画出的，也常常出现失败测试（失败的突破），形成很好的顺势入场。其中许多都是1分钟图上的高2/低2建仓形态，但当你在5分钟图上看到这些假突破时，并不需要再去看1分钟图，如图 2.7所示。


> Small trendlines in strong trends, even when drawn using adjacent bars, often have failure tests (failed breakouts) that set up good With Trend entries. Many of these are High/Low 2 setups on 1-minute charts, but you don't need to look at the 1-minute when you see the false breakouts on the 5-minute chart, as seen in Figure 2.7.


交易时，你并不需要经常真的在图上把趋势线画出来，因为大多数不用线帮忙也能看出来。


> When trading, you do not have to actually draw the trendlines on the chart very often because most are visible without the help of the lines.


1分钟 Emini 一整天都在趋势线测试、以及趋势通道过靶和反转处提供入场点。图 2.8中许多穿透都不到一个最小报价单位，但依然有意义。图中显示的线只是这张图上能画出的其中一部分，另外还有很多。


> The 1-minute Emini provided entries on trendline tests and trend channel overshoots and reversals all day long. Many of the penetrations in Figure 2.8 were less than one tick but still meaningful. The lines shown are just some of the ones that could be drawn on this chart, and there are many others.


每一条后续的趋势线都变得更平缓，直到另一个方向的趋势线主导了价格行为。


> Each successive trendline gets shallower until trendlines in the other direction dominate the price action.


在图 2.9中，今天有许多微型趋势线和通道交易（只显示四个），这是一个非常不寻常的日子：道指下跌超过700点，却一路反弹到收盘，收回了跌幅的一半。


> In Figure 2.9, there were many Micro Trendline and Channel trades today (only four are shown), a very unusual day where the Dow was down over 700 points but rallied into the close to make back half of the loss.


第5根K线是一次微型趋势通道反转，其中的通道线是第1到第4根K线微型趋势线的平行线。你也可以用低点（第1根K线和第3根K线之后那几根K线的低点）来画这条通道线。


> Bar 5 is a Micro Trend Channel reversal where the channel line was a parallel of the Bars 1 to 4 Micro Trendline. You could also have drawn the channel line using the lows (the lows of the bars after Bar 1 and Bar 3).


![图 2.8](figures/fig-02-08.png)


**图 2.8　趋势线测试与趋势通道的过靶和反转**


这里有一个很好的 ii形态（内包内包）建仓形态，两根K线都是多头收盘，这在反向操作强空头时总是理想的。


> There was a great ii setup where both bars had bull closes, which is always desirable when fading a strong bear.


第7根和第9根K线是微型趋势线假突破的做空剥头皮（低1建仓形态），随后两者都很快跟着买入剥头皮——因为失败本身也失败了，实际形成了突破回调买入（尽管两者都是更低的低点）以及最终旗形失败（从第7根和第9根K线那两根单K线熊旗中突破出来）。


> Bars 7 and 9 were Micro Trendline false breakout short scalps (Low 1 setups) and both were quickly followed by buy scalps as the failure failed, creating effectively a Breakout Pullback buy (even though both were Lower Lows) and a Failed Final Flag (the breakout from the one bar bear flags of Bars 7 and 9).


![图 2.9](figures/fig-02-09.png)


**图 2.9　微型趋势线：大波动日里的许多剥头皮机会**


从第5根K线开始的上涨行情测试了均线并突破了一条趋势线，所以买家在寻找测试第5根K线低点时的第二次入场做多。这里是更低的低点，第10根K线是在打掉第5根K线低点之后、第二次尝试上涨。这个更低的低点比第5根K线低点低得太多，距离那段突破趋势线的上涨行情（第1根到第4根K线那段行情的延伸）也太久，因此不算理想，但它仍然是一次带收涨信号K线的二次入场，也是微型趋势线突破失败之后的失败后的失败。


> The rally from Bar 5 tested the EMA and broke a trendline so buyers were looking for a second entry long on a test of the Bar 5 low. Here, it was a Lower Low and Bar 10 was a second attempt to rally after taking out the Bar 5 low. This Lower Low was too far below the Bar 5 low and too long after the rally that broke the trendline (an extension of that from Bars 1 to 4) to be ideal, but it was still a second entry with a signal bar with an up close, and a failed failure of a Micro Trendline break.


顺带一提，注意虽然图上没有画，但从第5根K线低点起有一条多头微型趋势线，6根K线之后那根小空头趋势K线突破了它。随后是对这个小多头极值点的更高的高点测试，然后是向下的趋势反转（在空头中，从均线上反转下来）。这里涉及的价格行为与主要趋势反转相同：一段趋势、一次趋势线突破、一次趋势极值点的测试（市场再次试图推高到那个价格区域之上），然后是市场在这次二次尝试中失败、行情反转。当市场试图做某件事两次都失败时，通常接着就会试图做相反的事。


> Incidentally, note that although not drawn, there is a bull Micro Trendline up from the Bar 5 low and the small bear trend bar 6 bars later broke it. This was followed by a Higher High test of the extreme of this small bull and then a trend reversal down (off the EMA in a bear). The price action involved is the same as for a major trend reversal: a trend, a trendline break, a test of the trend's extreme as the market once again tries to push above that price area, and then a reversal as the market fails in this second attempt. When the market tries to do something twice and fails, it usually then tries to do the opposite.


第11根K线是一个经典的陷阱，用来把你从一段强劲的上涨行情中震出来。如果你被震出局了，就必须在第11根K线微型趋势线假突破上方的高1处再次买入。


> Bar 11 was a classic trap to get you out of a strong rally. If you exited, you must buy again on the High 1 above the Bar 11 Micro Trendline false breakout.


今天许多K线的波幅都超过6到8点。明智的做法是把仓位规模减少到一半或更小，并把止损放大到4点、把止盈目标扩展到2点。除此之外，这不过又是一个规规矩矩的价格行为日。在大多数日子里——也就是交易区间日——横跨摆动高点和低点的水平线常常充当障碍，导致突破失败然后反转。要预期摆动高点的突破会失败并形成更高的高点，摆动低点的突破会失败并形成更低的低点。有时候失败本身也会失败，市场会创出第二次、更极端的更高的高点或更低的低点。反向操作第二次更高的高点或更低的低点建仓形态甚至更可能成功，因为其中许多都是三次推进形态的变体。


> Many of the bars today had a range of over 6 to 8 points. It would be prudent to reduce your position size to half or less, and increase your stop to 4 points and your profit target to 2 points. Otherwise, it was just another well-behaved price action day. On most days, which are trading range days, horizontal lines across swing . highs and lows often serve as barriers that result in failed breakouts and then reversals. Expect swing high breakouts to fail and form Higher Highs, and swing low breakouts to fail and form Lower Lows. Sometimes the failure fails, and the market makes a second more extreme Higher High or Lower Low. A fade of a second Higher High or Lower Low setup is even more likely to be successful because many of them are variants of Three Push patterns.


在趋势日里，水平线一般只应该用于在回调中入场，比如双顶熊旗或双底牛旗形态那样。一旦出现了明确的趋势线突破，对极值点的一次失败测试就能成为很好的反转建仓形态，尤其是在有强反转K线和二次入场（一个高2/低2）的时候。


> On trend days, horizontal lines should generally only be used to enter on pullbacks, like with the Double Top Bear Flag or a Double Bottom Bull Flag patterns. Once there has been a clear trendline break, a failed test of the extreme can be a good reversal setup, especially if there is a strong reversal bar and a second entry (a High/Low 2).


大多数日子并不是强趋势日，在这些日子里，交易者应该关注先前所有的摆动高点和低点，寻找失败测试和反转入场机会。高2/低2入场是最好的。第二次更高的高点或更低的低点，是在交易区间日里更极端的点位，而交易区间日的当天中段像一块磁力位，所以再创一个极值点更容易产生剥头皮交易者的利润。例如，图 2.10中的第5根K线是超过第2根K线的第二次更高的高点（也是从第3根K线起的三次推进向上）。


> Most days are not strong trend days, and on these days traders should be looking at all prior swing highs and lows for failed tests and reversal entries. High/Low 2 entries are the best. A second Higher High or Lower Low is a more extreme point on a trading range day where the middle of the day acts like a magnet, and a further extreme is therefore more likely to yield a scalper's profit. For example, Bar 5 in Figure 2. 10 is a second Higher High over Bar 2 (and Three Pushes up from Bar 3).


![图 2.10](figures/fig-02-10.png)


**图 2.10　水平线趋势线的突破失败**


第9根K线是低于当天开盘价的更低的低点（也是扩张三角形底部的第七个点）。


> Bar 9 is a Lower Low below the open of the day (and the seventh point of an Expanding Triangle Bottom).


第13根K线是一次大的双底回调（标注双底时有多个底部可选，第3根和第9根K线也许是最合适的）。


> Bar 13 is a large Double Bottom Pullback (there were multiple bottoms to choose from for labeling the Double Bottom, and Bars 3 and 9 might be the best).


第15根K线是双顶熊旗。当它失败时，市场明显变得更多头了。


> Bar 15 is a Double Top Bear Flag. When it failed, the market became noticeably more bullish.


第17根K线是低于第14根K线的第二次更低的低点，也是低于第16根K线的更低的低点。


> Bar 17 is a second Lower Low below Bar 14 and a Lower Low below Bar 16.


图 2.11 里那两天都是强趋势日，一个极值点出现在开盘附近，随后两个多小时没有回调到均线（2HM（两小时未触均线）日）。在强趋势日里，只有在首先出现了好的趋势线突破时，才考虑反向操作多头中的摆动高点、空头中的摆动低点。可接受的逆势入场出现在第4、8、12根K线。不过，既然这些是逆势交易，而趋势线突破处的逆势动能又很小，这些交易就只应该做剥头皮。如果它们让你分心、耽误了顺势入场——而你本来应该在那些顺势入场里用大部分仓位做波段交易——那就不要做。


> Both days were strong trend days in Figure 2.1 1 with one extreme near the open and then no EMA pullback for over two hours (2HM days). On strong trend days, only consider fading swing highs in bulls and swing lows in bears if there was first a good trendline break. Acceptable Countertrend entries were at Bars 4, 8, and 12. However, since these are Countertrend and there was only minimal Countertrend momentum on the trendline breaks, these trades should only be scalps. Do not take them if they are distracting you from the With Trend entries, where you should swing much of your position.


第1根和第5根K线形成了双底牛旗，第9根K线是双顶熊旗的一部分。


> Bars 1 and 5 formed a Double Bottom Bull Flag, and Bar 9 was part of a Double Top Bear Flag.


![图 2.11](figures/fig-02-11.png)


**图 2.11　只有在首先出现趋势线突破时，才做逆势交易**


第5根和第13根K线都提供了很好的顺势入场（均线缺口K线、11:30时段的陷阱），依据是摆动点上的反向操作（第5根K线是摆动低点突破的反向操作，第13根K线是摆动高点突破的反向操作）。趋势通道线位于趋势线另一侧的价格行为之外，斜率大体相同。在多头中，趋势线在低点下方，趋势通道线在高点上方，两者都向右上方倾斜。趋势通道线是一个有用的工具，用来反向操作走得太远、太快的趋势。寻找过靶之后反转的情形，尤其是过靶的第二次反转。


> Both Bars 5 and 13 gave great With Trend entries (EMA Gap bars, 1 1:30 traps) based on swing fades (Bar 5 was a swing low breakout fade, and Bar 13 is a swing high breakout fade). Trend channel lines are on the opposite side of the price action from a trendline and have the same general slope. In a bull, a trendline is below the lows and a trend channel line is above the highs, and both are rising up and to the right. A trend channel line is a useful tool to fade a trend that has gone too far, too fast. Look for an overshoot that reverses, especially if it is a second reversal of the overshoot.


通常来说，当存在趋势时，你总能找到一条趋势线和一条趋势通道线把它包住。市场最终会朝任一方向突破通道。大多数趋势通道线过靶都会反转回到通道内，但有时候某一次会继续走下去，结果形成更陡的趋势。同样，大多数趋势线突破都会失败，但它们会产生一个新的摆动点，从而画出一条新的、坡度更小的趋势线，说明趋势可能已经变弱。最终会出现一次趋势线突破，它远远越过趋势线、动能又如此之强，以至于这波急冲之后的回调无法超过先前的趋势极值点。这个摆动点（新多头中的更高的低点，或新空头中的更低的高点）可以用旧趋势的终点作起点、为刚起步的趋势画一条趋势线。随着新趋势的发展，它自己的趋势线和趋势通道线比旧趋势的那些线更能体现正在发生的事，于是它们就成了你交易时的焦点。既然大多数趋势线和趋势通道线的突破都会失败，在突破处入场就是亏钱的策略。在失败处入场要赚钱得多，但如果突破延伸得很远，那就应该等回调，然后顺着突破方向入场。


> Usually 'When there is a trend, you can find a trendline and a trend channel line that contain it. The market will eventually break out of the channel in either direction. Most trend channel line overshoots reverse back into the channel but sometimes one will continue and this results in a steeper trend. Also, most trendline breaks fail but they generate a new swing point that creates a new, less steep trendline, indicating that the trend may have become weaker, Eventually, there will be a trendline break that extends so far beyond the trendline and has so much momentum that the pullback from this surge will fail to exceed the prior trend extreme. This swing point (a Higher Low in a new bull or a Lower High in a new bear) can be used to draw a trendline for the incipient trend, using the end of the old trend as the first point of the trendline. As the new trend develops, its trendlines and trend channel lines represent what is taking place better than the lines from the old trend and they become the focus of your trading. Since most trendline and trend channel line breakouts fail, entering on the breakouts is a losing strategy. It is far more profitable to look to enter on the failure, but if the breakout extends far, then you should wait for a pullback and then enter in the direction of the breakout.


趋势通道线可以是一条与趋势线平行的线并拖到价格行为的另一侧，也可以横跨另一侧的急速行情来画，还可以是一条最佳拟合线，比如回归线，或者目测画一条最佳拟合线。在多头中，趋势线横跨两个低点画出。如果这条趋势线被用来构造趋势通道线，就把它拖到趋势的另一侧。你要让它包含（位于其上方）画趋势线所用的两根K线之间所有K线的高点，所以就把它拖到某一根K线的高点上，使得它只碰到这一根K线。偶尔，把线锚定在画趋势线所用两根K线之外的某根K线上，你会对趋势有更好的理解。永远都要选最能突出趋势的画法。


> A trend channel line can be a parallel to a trendline and dragged to the opposite side of the price action, it can be drawn across spikes on that opposite side, or it can be a best fit line, like a regression line or visually drawing a best fit line. In a bull, a trendline is drawn across two lows. If that trendline is used to form a trend channel line, then drag it to the opposite side of the trend. You want it to contain (be above) the highs of all of the bars located in between the two bars used to create the trendline, so drag it to the high of whatever bar that will leave it touching that bar alone. Occasionally you will get a better sense of the trend if you anchor the line to a bar that is outside of the two bars. Always do whatever best highlights the trend.


另一种做法是，趋势通道线独立画出来也很有用。在空头波段中，趋势线向下倾斜，位于高点上方。趋势通道线的斜率类似，但把它画在空头波段中任意两个摆动低点之间。如果它包含（位于其下方）该波段中所有其他K线，那就最有用，所以要挑选能给出这个结果的那些K线。


> Alternatively, a trend channel line can be useful when created on its own. In a bear swing, a trendline will be downward sloping and above the highs. The trend channel line will have a similar slope, but draw it between any two swing lows in the bear swing. It is most useful if it contains (is below) all of the other bars in the swing, so choose the bars that will give that result.


趋势通道线过靶与楔形密切相关，应该把它们看成同一个东西来看待和交易。大多数楔形都以这条通道线的突破失败作为反转交易的触发点，而大多数趋势通道过靶和反转同时也是楔形反转，尽管那个楔形可能并不明显，或者没有完美的楔形形状。当趋势通道线是以趋势线的平行线方式构造出来时，楔形没那么明显、出现的可能性也更小，但楔形仍然常常存在。


> Trend channel line overshoots are closely related to Wedges and should be viewed and traded as if they are one and the same. Most Wedges have failed trend channel breakouts as the trigger for a reversal trade, and most trend channel overshoots and reversals are also Wedge reversals, although the Wedge may not be obvious or have a perfect Wedge shape. The Wedges are less obvious and less likely to be present when the trend channel line is constructed as a parallel of a trendline, but Wedges are still often present.


既然人人都知道趋势通道线过靶常常导致反转，为什么还会有这么多反转发生在过靶之后？抢先入场的人难道不会让价格根本到不了这条线吗？常见的说法是，站错方向的新手交易者会一直扛着亏损的持仓，直到再也忍受不了痛苦，然后所有人突然一下子同时离场，造出一波急冲或抛物线高潮。然而，在 Emini 这样的大市场里，这并不是反转的一个有分量的组成部分。聪明的交易者不会去做逆势，除非要么出现了来自一段强趋势线突破之后的回调，要么出现了来自趋势通道线过靶的反转。例如，在多头中，精明资金会一直买入，直到把价格推升到多头趋势通道线之上，然后才止盈。


> Why do so many reversals occur after trend channel line overshoots when everyone knows that it commonly leads to a reversal? Won't early entrants prevent the line from ever being reached? Common wisdom is that novice traders on the wrong side hold their losing positions until they cannot stand any more pain, and then suddenly all of them exit at once, creating a blow-off or a parabolic climax. However, that is not a meaningful component of a reversal in a huge market like the Eminis. Smart traders won't trade Countertrend until either there is a pullback from a strong trendline break or there is a reversal from a trend channel line overshoot. For example, in a bull, smart money will keep buying until they drive the price above the bull trend channel line, and then they will take profits.


一路上可能会有几次失败，然后一条更长、更陡的线开始起作用，但市场最终会就哪一条是最终的那条线达成一致。在止盈者止盈的同时，许多人会反手，另外许多本来空仓的人会开始做空。其他聪明的交易者会等图表上出现反转，而且会有人在各种类型的图表上于反转处入场（1到5分钟图，以及任何大小的量图和 tick 图）。


> There may be a couple of failures along the way and then a longer and steeper line comes into play, but eventually the market will agree on which line is the final one. At the same time as the profit takers are taking profits, many will reverse, and many others who were already flat will initiate shorts. Other smart traders will wait for a reversal on the charts and there will be traders entering on reversals on all types of charts (1- to 5-minute, and volume charts and tick chart of any size).


一旦他们相信顶部已经形成，这些精明资金就不会再想着买入了。他们持有空头，其中许多人会扛过新高，尽管当前持仓是浮亏，因为他们相信顶部已经形成或接近形成。事实上，许多人会在高点上方加仓，既能给自己空头拿到更好的均价，也有助于把市场压下去。大玩家满脑子只想做空，除非出现罕见的二次入场失败或一次大失败（例如，也许在他们入场价上方3点），否则不会被吓出去。已经没有买家了，所以市场只剩下一个方向可走。


> Once they believe that the top is in, this smart money won't be looking to buy any longer. They are short, and many of these traders will hold through a new high, despite an open loss on their current position, believing that the top is in or close to in. In fact, many will add on above the high, both to get a better average price for their shorts and to help push the market down. The big players are only thinking short and won't be scared out except by the rare occurrence of a failed second entry or a huge failure (for example, maybe three points above their entry). There are no buyers left so the market only has one way to go.


看看关键转折点处的成交量。它巨大。唯一合乎逻辑的解释是：机构在一个方向上离场、同时在另一个方向上入场，而另一些机构作为另一个市场（股票、期权、债券、外汇等等）对冲的一部分，接下相反的那一边。他们认为在高点买入期货、或在低点卖出期货、再在另一个市场对冲掉风险，自己的风险回报比更好。除此之外都说不通。你要知道，这些成交量不是小散户被挤出空头、在高点买入造成的。这世上有的是蠢人，但就算把他们在高点的所有买单加在一起，相比机构成交量也还是微不足道。


> Look at the volume at key turning points. It's huge. The only logical way that can happen is if institutions are exiting in one direction and entering in the other, and other institutions are taking the opposite side as part of a hedge in another market (stocks, options, bonds, currencies, and so on). They perceive that their risk-reward ratio is better by buying futures at the high or selling them at the low and offsetting the risk in another market. Nothing else makes sense. You know that the volume is not from small individual traders being squeezed out of shorts and buying at the high. There are plenty of stupid people out there, but if you were to pool all of their buys at the high, it is still small compared to the institutional volume.


过靶处的反转之所以发生，是因为它已经深深植入机构交易者的心理，必定会发生。即使某家机构不看图表，它也会有别的标准告诉它市场已经走得太远、该离场或反手了，而这总会与价格行为交易者看到的东西吻合。记住，价格行为是价格身上正在发生的事所留下的、无法抹去的足迹——大量聪明人各自独立地想在市场里赚到尽可能多的钱。在一个大市场里，价格无法被操纵，而且总会基本保持一样。


> The reversal at an overshoot happens because it is such an entrenched part of institutional trading psyche that it has to happen. Even if an institution does not look at charts, it will have some other criterion that tells them that the market has gone too far and it is time to exit or reverse, and this will invariably coincide with what price action traders are seeing. Remember, price action is the inescapable footprint of what is happening to price as a huge number of smart people are independently trying to make the most money that they can in the market. In a big market, it cannot be manipulated and will always be basically the same.


最后一个观察是：一段趋势的最终旗形的斜率，常常能大致给出新趋势的斜率。这对交易者的价值有限，因为在决定下单之前涉及的决策里，还有另外一些重要得多的因素，但这确实是个有趣的观察。


> One final observation is that the slope of the final flag of a trend often provides an approximation of the slope of the new trend. This has limited value to a trader because there will be other much more important factors involved in the decision leading up to placing a trade, but it is an interesting observation.


把它们向右延伸，观察价格在穿透通道线时如何表现。


> Extend them to the right and watch how the price acts when it penetrates the channel line.


![图 2.12](figures/fig-02-12.png)


**图 2.12　趋势通道线指向趋势方向，但位于与趋势线相反的一侧**


趋势通道线通常有两种画法。第一种，先作趋势线（实线）的平行线（图 2.12中的虚线），然后拖到行情另一侧，放置到画趋势线所用两根K线之间的某个摆动点上。挑选那个能让趋势线和通道线之间的所有K线都被包在两条线里面的点。第二种趋势通道线（点线）横跨摆动点画出，与任何趋势线无关。你也可以干脆画一条最佳拟合线，但这些在交易中通常没什么用。


> Trend channel lines are commonly drawn in one of two ways. First, as a parallel line (dashed line in Figure 2. 12) of a trendline (solid line) and then dragged to the opposite side of the action, placed to touch a swing point located between the two bars used to create the trendline. Choose the point that will result in all of the bars between the trend and channel lines being contained between the lines. The second type (dotted line) of trend channel line is drawn across swing points and is independent of any trendline. You can also simply draw a best fit, but these are usually not helpful in trading.


图 2.13中多头最终旗形的斜率为随后的空头提供了方向。在第1根和第2根K线之间画的一条线性回归趋势线，大致成了那波延续到下一个交易日的抛售行情的空头趋势通道线。它有可能促成了第7根K线处的买入，但第7根K线的买入单纯就是基于趋势线突破，以及第二次尝试反转跌破开盘价低点的那次突破。如果最近的价格行为能为交易提供理由，那么据此下单通常远比回头看30根或更多K线要好得多。


> The slope of the final flag of the bull in Figure 2. 13 provided direction for the subsequent bear. A linear regression trendline drawn between Bars 1 and 2 became a rough bear trend channel line for the selloff that extended into the next day. It is possible that it contributed to the buying at Bar 7, but Bar 7 was a buy simply based on the trendline break and the second attempt to reverse the breakout below the low of the open. It is usually far better to place orders based on the most recent price action if it provides a justification for a trade than to look back 30 or more bars.


图 2.14中第2根和第3根K线那条趋势线被用来作平行线，拖到第1根K线并向右延伸。这条趋势通道线（点线）没有被第5根K线穿透。而且，它锚定在第1根K线上，而第1根K线并不在画原趋势线所用的第2根和第3根K线之间。不过，交易者应该永远考虑每一种可能性。如果真出现了穿透和反转，那么从第5根K线低点起走出两段式上涨行情的可能性就会提高。


> The trendline from Bars 2 and 3 in Figure 2. 14 was used to create a parallel that was dragged to Bar 1 and extended to the right. This trend channel line (dotted) was not penetrated by Bar 5. Also, it was anchored to Bar 1, which is not in between Bars 2 and 3, the bars used to create the original trendline. However, traders should always be looking at every possibility. Had there been a penetration and reversal, the chances of a two-legged rally off the Bar 5 low would be improved.


![图 2.13](figures/fig-02-13.png)


**图 2.13　最终旗形的斜率常常决定新趋势的斜率**


用第1根和第5根K线画的那条简单趋势通道线被第6根K线穿透了，但这不是一条用作逆势交易依据的理想趋势通道线，因为第1根和第5根K线相距太远，而第5根和第6根K线又靠得太近。趋势线在被第三段行情测试时效果最好，而这里第5根和第6根K线基本上仍然是同一段行情的一部分（三次推进向下，第4、5、6根K线）。这笔交易仍然值得做，因为第6根K线很小，所以风险回报比很好。这也是一个向下的收缩楼梯形态，说明空头动能正在减弱，支持做多。当一条较长的趋势线被测试，而测试发生在一条斜率相反的较短时间级别趋势通道线处时，如果测试成功（突破失败并反转），就应该考虑顺着趋势方向入场。趋势通道线测试说明修正已经结束，位置也很理想，因为它测试的是一条较长的趋势线。


> The simple trend channel line using Bars 1 and 5 was penetrated by Bar 6, but this is not an ideal trend channel line to use as a basis for a Countertrend trade since Bars 1 and 5 were far apart and Bars 5 and 6 were close together. Trendlines work best when they are tested by a third leg, and here Bars 5 and 6 were essentially still part of the same leg (Three Pushes Down, Bars 4, 5, and 6). The trade was still worth taking because Bar 6 was small, so the risk reward ratio was good. This is also a Shrinking Stair pattern down, which indicates waning bearish momentum and supports a long. When a longer trendline is tested and the test occurs at a shorter-term trend channel line of opposite slope, look to enter in the direction of the trend if the test is successful (failed breakout and reversal). The trend channel line test indicates that the correction is over and the location is perfect, since it is a test of a longer trendline.


![图 2.14](figures/fig-02-14.png)


**图 2.14　趋势通道线的一个变体**


图 2.15中从第3根和第5根K线画出的空头趋势通道线在第6根K线处提供了支撑。第3根K线是多头中的一个摆动低点，第5根K线看起来是新空头中的一个摆动低点。然而，跌到第6根K线的那段运动只是多头市场里一次大的两段式修正。第6根K线处出现了决斗线（一条多头趋势线和一条斜率相反的空头趋势通道线），而市场在交叉处反转向上，这很常见。由于跌到第6根K线的运动很陡，等第7根K线那个更高的低点处的二次入场是合理的，在其高点上方一个最小报价单位处挂止损单买入。


> A bear trend channel line drawn from Bars 3 and 5 in Figure 2. 15 offered support at Bar 6. Bar 3 was a swing low in a bull, and Bar 5 appeared to be a swing low in a new bear. However, the move down to Bar 6 was just a large two-legged correction in the bull market. There were Dueling Lines at Bar 6 (a bull trendline and a bear trend channel line of opposite slope), and the market reversed up at the intersection, as is common. Since the move down to Bar 6 was steep, it is reasonable to wait for the second entry at the Bar 7 Higher Low, buying on a stop at one tick over its high.


![图 2.15](figures/fig-02-15.png)


**图 2.15　画趋势线和趋势通道线时应该考虑所有摆动点，哪怕来自先前趋势的那些**


![图 2.16](figures/fig-02-16.png)


**图 2.16　决斗线**


空头趋势通道线也可以基于一条连接第4根K线高点之后那两个摆动高点的趋势线画出，然后锚定到第5根K线。目标是先看整体形状，然后选一条能包含价格行为的趋势通道线。接着，观察市场在穿透这条线之后如何反应。


> A bear trend channel line could also have been based on a trendline drawn across the two swing highs that followed the Bar 4 high, and then anchored to Bar 5. The goal is to look at the overall shape and then choose any trend channel line that contains the price action. Then, watch how the market reacts after penetrating the line.


图 2.16中的第4根K线测试了空头趋势线，而在测试的同时，一条更小的多头趋势通道线（从第3根到第4根K线）出现了过靶，结果带来了一笔基于决斗线形态的做空剥头皮。第6根K线那个名义更高的高点处出现了二次入场。


> Bar 4 in Figure 2.16 tested the bear trendline and as it did, there was an overshoot of a smaller bull trend channel line (from Bars 3 to 4), resulting in a short scalp off the Dueling Lines pattern. There was a second entry at the Bar 6 nominal Higher High.


# 第 3 章　趋势

*Chapter 3. Trends*


为什么识别趋势是否存在很重要？因为一旦确认，你的大多数交易就都应当顺着那个方向；你必须尽量抓住每一次顺势入场，而很少做逆势入场。你越早看出趋势，能赚到的钱就越多。把注意力放在逆势建仓形态上，很可能让你错过那些利润丰厚得多、但往往更吓人的顺势入场。顺势入场之所以吓人，是因为市场看起来总是走过了头，你很难想象在一轮过头的空头趋势低点附近卖出、或在一轮过头的多头趋势高点附近买入，居然还能赚钱。可恰恰就是这样，它才赚钱！市场会把逆势交易者吸引进来，而如果你在它们亏损离场的位置入场，它们就会推着市场朝你的方向走——哪怕市场看上去已经过分延伸。本章讲的是许多常见的趋势形态，你每天都该留意。如果这些形态在当天的头一两个小时里开始成形，接下来很可能有好几笔高概率的顺势交易可做。你每天都要反复判断：今天是否像本章后面描述的某一类趋势？如果像，那就逼着自己去做那些顺势交易。


> Why is it important to recognize the existence of a trend? Because then most of your trades should be in that direction and you must try to take every With Trend entry and rarely take Countertrend entries, The earlier you see the trend, the more money you stand to make. Focusing on the Countertrend setups will likely make you miss the much more profitable but often scarier With Trend entries. The With Trend entries are scary because the market always looks overdone and it's hard to imagine that selling near the low of an overdone bear or buying near the high of an overdone bull could ever be profitable. However, that is exactly why it is! The market draws in Countertrend traders, and if you enter where they exit at a loss, they will drive the market in your direction, even though the market looks so overextended. This chapter describes many common trend patterns that you should look for every day. If you see one setting up within the first hour or two of the day, there will likely be several high probability With Trend trades that you can then make. You need to decide many times every day if the day resembles any of the types of trends described later in this chapter, and if it does, force yourself to take the With Trend trades.


趋势是一连串价格变化，它们主要是向上（多头趋势，也就是多头）或者向下（空头趋势，也就是空头）。趋势可以短到只有一根K线（记住，一根趋势K线就是更小时间级别上的一段趋势），也可以长过你屏幕上的所有K线。趋势被粗略地分成四个彼此重叠、常常可以互换的类别：趋势、波段、回调、行情段。这些区分只是指导性的，因为后三个较小的称呼在不同时间级别上指的都是不同的东西。


> A trend is a series of price changes that are mostly either up (a bull trend or a bull) or down (a bear trend or a bear). A trend can be as short as a single bar (remember, a trend bar is made up of a trend on a smaller time frame) or longer than all of the bars on your screen. Trends are loosely classified into four overlapping and often interchangeable categories: trend, swing, pullback, and leg. The distinctions are just guidelines because each of the three smaller versions is a different version on different time frames.


例如，60分钟图上多头行情里的一次回调，在1分钟图上可能是一段强劲的空头趋势。此外，每一类里都会包含一个或多个更小的类别。一段趋势可能由10个波段组成，每个波段包含1到4次回调，而每次回调又可能有1到4段行情段。另外，任何规模的上涨波段和下跌波段通常都被叫作行情段，所以这些区分并不太重要，但每个叫法都带着一点细微的差别。


> For example, a pullback in a bull on a 60-minute chart might be a strong bear trend on a 1-minute chart. Also, each category will contain one or more of the smaller versions. A trend might be made of 10 swings, each containing 1 to 4 pullbacks, and each pullback might have 1 to 4 legs. Also, every up and downswing of any size is commonly referred to a leg, so the distinctions are not very important, but each term carries a subtle distinction with it.


最简单的判断是：如果你电脑屏幕上的图从一个左角开始，斜着走到屏幕对角，中间没有巨大的起伏，趋势就存在。例如，左边的K线靠近显示器左下角，右边的K线靠近右上角，而屏幕中间没有多少大幅的上涨和下跌，那这就是多头趋势。一张图只呈现一到两个趋势。


> At its simplest, a trend is present when the chart on your computer screen starts at one of the two left-hand comers and ends at the diagonally opposite comer of the screen with no huge fluctuation in between. For example, if the bars on the left are near the lower left comer of your monitor and the bars on the right are near the upper right-hand comer and there are not many large upswings and downswings in the middle of your screen, then this is a bull trend. A chart only shows one or two trends.


如果一张图上出现了两个以上的趋势，最好改用另外三个类别中的一个来描述，因为双向运行会带来不同的交易机会。波段和行情段都是更小的趋势，而一张图上至少会有两个。当一张图上有两个或更多更小的趋势时，就用“波段”这个词——哪怕整张图可能是横盘。


> If more than two trends are present on a chart, it is preferable to describe the trends by using one of the other three classifications because the two-sided action creates different trading opportunities. Both swings and legs are smaller trends, and there are at least two on the chart. The term swing is used when there are two or more smaller trends on the chart, even though the overall chart might be sideways.


行情段是更大趋势里的任何一段更小的趋势；它可以是回调（一段逆势行情），可以是趋势里或横盘市场里的一个波段，也可以是趋势内部任意两次回调之间的顺势行情。


> A leg is any smaller trend that is part of a larger trend, and it can be a pullback (a Countertrend move), a swing in a trend or in a sideways market, or a With Trend move that occurs between any two pullbacks within a trend.


回调是一段临时的逆势行情，它属于某段趋势、波段或行情段。例如，多头回调就是多头趋势、波段或行情段中一段横盘到向下的行情，之后至少会去测试先前的高点。任何代表停顿或动能丧失的一根或一连串K线都是回调，即使价格实际上并没有往回走。这包括单独一根内包K线——显然，它既没有跌破前一根K线的低点，也没有涨过前一根K线的高点。当回调只有一根K线时，这根K线叫停顿K线（Pause Bar）或回调K线（Pullback Bar）。这些单根K线的回调，在更小时间级别的图上由一连串小波段组成。不过，你可能得一路看到1分钟图、100 tick 图甚至更小的图才能看见它们。对交易者来说这是浪费时间，但了解这个事实很有帮助，因为它为考虑下单提供了一个理由。


> A pullback is a temporary Countertrend move and is part of a trend, swing, or leg. For example, a bull pullback is a sideways to downward move in a bull trend, swing, or leg that will be followed by at least a test of the prior high. Any bar or series of bars that represents any pause or loss of momentum is a pullback, even if there is no actual backward movement. This includes a single inside bar, which obviously does not extend below the low or above the high of the prior bar. When it is a single bar, the bar is called a Pause Bar or a Pullback Bar. These one-bar pullbacks are made up of a series of small swings on a smaller time frame chart. However, you might have to go all of the way down to a 1-minute or a 100 tick or smaller chart to see them. This is a waste of time for a trader, but it is helpful to be aware of the reality because it provides a rationale for considering placing a trade.


任何趋势内部都有许多更小的反向趋势，有些只持续一两根K线；这些反向趋势都应当被看作很可能失败，因此也就是顺着更大趋势方向入场的建仓形态。在多头行情里，波段应当依次抬高，也就是说每一次回调都应当高于前一次回调，并且应当带来新高（高点与低点依次推进，或者波段依次推进）。所有动能强劲的行情，在回调之后通常至少会有一次对极值的测试（所有强势行情通常至少有两段，即使第二段没走够就反转了）。


> Within any trend, there are a number of smaller opposite trends, some lasting for only one or two bars, and all of them should be considered as likely to fail and therefore setups for trades in the direction of the larger trend. In a bull, the swings should be trending upward, meaning that each pullback should be above the prior pullback, and it should result in a new high (trending highs and lows, or trending swings). All moves with strong momentum usually have at least a test of the extreme following a pullback (all strong moves usually have at least two legs, even if the second one falls short and reverses).


所有趋势，无论多小，都必须先突破前一段趋势或交易区间画出的趋势线，然后走出依次推进的波段（比如多头行情里一连串更高的高点和更低的低点）。这两条缺了任何一条，就谈不上趋势。最好的风险回报比出现在趋势线突破之后的第一波回调上——那时趋势还没有明确确立。当一个可能的趋势日正在展开时，交易者应当寻找强势迹象，每一个强势迹象都会提高趋势延续的概率。


> All trends, no matter how small, must first break a trendline from the prior trend or trading range and then have trending swings (such as a series of Higher Highs and Lows in a bull). Absent either of these, there is no trend. The best risk reward ratio occurs when you enter on the First Pullback after a trendline break, before there is a clearly established trend. As a possible trend day is unfolding, traders should look for signs of strength, each of which increases the odds that the trend will continue.


趋势会一直延续到突破自己的趋势线之后，而且突破之后往往还会再延续一段。在市场有足够力量突破趋势线之前，你不该做逆势交易。不过，即便到了那时候，也要等市场先回去测试趋势的极值，你才该做逆势入场。这意味着，即使趋势线已经被突破，你仍然应当寻找顺势交易，因为通常还会有一次对老极值的测试。有时趋势线突破时力量太强，对趋势极值的测试就会很小，但这是例外，不是常态。


> The trend continues until after it breaks its trendline, and then it continues some more. You should not be trading countertrend until the market has enough strength to break the trendline. However, even then, you should not be entering countertrend until the market first goes back to test the extreme of the trend. This means that even after a trendline break, you should still be looking for With Trend trades because there should be a test of the old extreme. Sometimes there is so much strength on the trendline break that there should not be much of a test of the trend extreme, but this is the exception and not the rule.


如果你发现自己画了一堆趋势通道线，或者盯上了1分钟图，那说明你太急于找反转，很可能正在错过大量绝佳的顺势交易。你在自欺欺人，并因此亏钱。另外，在强趋势里，大多数趋势通道线过靶和反转都很小、都会失败，于是你会做一大堆亏损交易，还会纳闷：这些形态本该这么好，为什么老是失败？要在5分钟图上等趋势线被突破之后，再去找逆势交易；把那些小的趋势通道线过靶全都看成顺势建仓形态，在那些亏损者按保护性止损离场的位置入场。你会快乐得多、放松得多、也富有得多；而且你会觉得很有意思：这些交易从直觉上看根本不该管用——因为市场看起来已经走得太远、早就该修正了——可它们偏偏很管用。


> If you find yourself drawing many trend channel lines or looking at a 1-minute chart, then you are too eager to find a reversal and are likely missing lots of great With Trend trades. You are in denial and are losing money because of it. Also, since most trend channel line overshoots and reversals are minor in a strong trend and fail, you will be trading lots of losers and wondering why these patterns are failing when they are supposed to be so good. Wait for a trendline break on the 5-minute chart before looking for a countertrend trade and look at all those minor trend channel line overshoots as With Trend setups, and enter where the losers are exiting on their protective stops. You will be much happier, relaxed, and richer, and you will be entertained by how well they work when intuitively they should not because the market appears to have gone much too far without a correction.


每当你发现自己为了等一次漂亮的反转而等了很久，你就是对眼前这段趋势视而不见。当趋势强到根本碰不到趋势线，而你觉得它已经走得太远、认为在极值附近顺势入场太冒险时，你正在错过市场上最可靠的交易。所有小幅回调——哪怕只是一根小小的内包K线——都是极好的顺势入场点。


> Whenever you find yourself waiting a long time for a great reversal, you are oblivious to the trend that is in front of you. When a trend is that strong that it cannot get anywhere near a trendline but you feel it has gone much too far, and you think that entering With Trend near the extreme is risky, you are missing the most reliable trades that exist. All minor pullbacks, even a single, small inside bar, are great With Trend entries.


在日线图上，空头市场大幅下跌之后，人们开始非常担心已经亏掉的钱，不愿再亏更多。这让他们不问基本面就卖出。2008年的空头行情里还多了一个问题：婴儿潮一代正处在退休边缘，眼看着自己心里那份安稳的养老钱迅速缩水40%，他们吓坏了。那他们会怎么做？他们会继续在每一次反弹中卖出，努力保住剩下的东西。而且，他们从市场里撤走的那些钱，再也不会回来推高价格了。一路上那些“感谢上帝”式的点位，就是他们把钱取走的地方——那正是前一个摆动高点下方一点：他们在这里离场，并向上帝许诺，只要让他收回一部分损失，他就再也不买了。这样就形成了一连串更低的高点和更低的低点，直到最后一个空头卖光为止。那之后，市场才能反弹到前一个摆动高点之上。


> After a substantial decline in a bear market on the daily chart, people begin to become very concerned about the money that they've lost and they do not want to lose any more money. This makes them sell, regardless of the fundamentals. There was an added problem in the bear of 2008. Baby Boomers were on the verge of retiring and were shocked by what they saw as comfortable nest eggs quickly falling 40 percent in value. So what will they do? They will continue to sell every rally as they try to preserve what they have left. Also, all that money that they are taking out of the market will never return to lift prices again. They will take their money at all the "Thank you, God" points along the way. This will be just below the prior swing high, where they exit and promise God that they will never buy again in return for him letting them recoup some of their losses. This creates a series of lower highs and lows until the last bear has sold. Once that happens, the market will then be able to rally above the prior swing high.


人们不问基本面就卖出，结果是市场常常走出巨大的空头趋势日，跌幅远超基本面应该支持的程度；而且经常在最后30分钟出现一次暴跌，因为基金被赎回指令逼着卖出。一路上还会出现凶猛的反弹：人们相信底部已经到了，慌忙重新做多。另外，因为趋势明确向下，做空的人很多，他们会凶狠地回补，在日线图上打出巨大的多头趋势K线——可市场仍然是空头市场。最终的结果是：空头行情一旦全面展开，就会出现一连串波幅极大的日子。这些巨大的波幅提供了极好的价格行为日内交易机会，但你也许得把止损的距离加大，从而把仓位规模减小。跟着日线图操作的人在每一个陷阱的低点卖出、高点买入（每一个陷阱都是一次强劲的空头回补反弹），凭情绪而不是凭理性交易；而一个不错的价格行为交易者只要寻找标准的价格行为建仓形态，就能做得非常好。


> The result of people selling regardless of fundamentals is that the market often falls in huge bear trend days, dropping much further than what the fundamentals warrant, and often there is a huge plunge in the final 30 minutes as funds are forced to sell because of redemption orders. There will be vicious rallies along the way as people become convinced that the bottom is in and they panic to get back long. Also, because the trend is so clearly down, there will be many who are short and will cover aggressively, resulting in huge bull trend bars on the daily chart, but still in a bear market. The end result is a collection of very large range days once the bear is well underway. The huge ranges offer great price action day trading opportunities but you might have to increase your stop size and therefore reduce your position size. While people following the daily charts are selling at the low and buying at the high of each trap (every strong short covering rally), trading off emotion more than reason, a good price action trader can do very well just looking for standard price action setups.


这种心态并不只出现在不成熟的投资者身上。2008年秋天，多数对冲基金当年都是亏的，随着市场持续抛售，它们那些老练的投资者也在凶狠地撤资。对冲基金不得不在每一次小幅反弹中继续变现，以应付赎回和预期中的赎回。这股力量与基本面无关，持续把市场往下压；和那些不太成熟的投资者一样，卖出会一直持续，直到剩下的全是投资者打算一直持有到归零的仓位为止。另外，对许多对冲基金经理来说，收入的一大块来自业绩激励。比如，基金每个季度只要以新高收官，他们就可能从超过原净值高点的利润里提走20%。反过来，如果基金当年亏了30%，它得赚回大约50% 才能重新回到那个激励线。与其白干好几年，关掉基金、重新起一只新基金更说得通。可是关基金就得清盘，而既然激励对他们已经不存在，他们可以用任何价格清盘，再低都行。这就又添了一份与股票内在价值无关的卖压。如果他们管理的是一只10亿美元的基金，新基金是从零开始，得花上几年才能拥有足够的净值和跟老基金一样多的股票，所以新基金的买入不会立刻把市场抬起来。


> This kind of mentality is not restricted to unsophisticated investors. In the fall of 2008, most hedge funds were down on the year and their sophisticated investors aggressively pulled their money out as the market continued to sell off. The hedge funds had to continue to liquidate on every small rally to meet redemptions and anticipated redemptions. This continued to drive the market down, independent of fundamentals, and just like with less sophisticated investors, the selling will continue until all that's left are positions that investors will hold until they fall to zero. Also, for many hedge fund managers a big part of their income is incentive-based. For example, every quarter that the fund closes at a new high, they might take 20 percent of that profit above the old equity high. If the fund instead is down 30 percent on the year, it will need to earn about 50 percent to get up to that incentive level again. Rather than working for free for several years, it might make more sense to close the fund and start over with a new fund. However, when they close the fund, they have to liquidate and since there is no incentive for them, they can liquidate at any price, no matter how low. This adds to selling that is independent of the intrinsic value of stocks. If they have a one billion dollar fund, their new fund is starting from scratch and it will take a few years before they have enough equity and own as much stock as they did in the old fund, so buying by the new funds don't immediately lift the market.


当波动性到达极值时，空头行情往往就快到尽头了：交易者不再理会来回拉锯，认定手里已经没有什么东西是他们愿意在任何价格上卖出的。当再没有卖家、而市场从基本面看也已经走过头时，随后应当会有一波像样的上涨行情。那么，一只知名股票在空头行情里究竟能跌多少？比你可能想象的还要远得多，即便是最蓝筹的蓝筹股也一样。CSCO 在2000年科技股崩盘后的三年里跌掉了90% 的市值，AAPL 在1991年之后的六年里跌掉了85%。GM 在2001年之后的八年里跌掉了95%。所以，别仅仅因为一只股票跌到了斐波那契的38%、50% 甚至62% 就急着买入。要等到出现价格行为建仓形态，而且这个形态必须包含此前对空头趋势线的一次突破。


> When the volatility reaches an extreme, the end of the bear is often near as traders give up responding to the whipsaws and decide that there is nothing left that they will sell at any price. When there are no more sellers and the market is overdone on the basis of fundamentals, a good rally should follow. And just how far can a big name stock fall in a bear? Much farther than you might think, even for the bluest of the blue chips. CSCO lost 90 percent of its value in three years after the tech wreck of 2000, and AAPL lost 85 percent of its value in the six years after 1991. GM lost 95 percent in the eight years after 2001.
